verses.1:1: The vision of Isaiah, son of Amoz, which he saw regarding Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
verses.1:2: Hear, heavens, and listen with your ears, earth, for the Lord has spoken: "I have nourished and exalted sons, yet they themselves have despised Me.
verses.1:3: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey the feeding trough of its master; yet Israel has not known Me, and My people have not understood."
verses.1:4: Woe to a sinful nation, a people heavy with iniquity, a wicked seed, depraved sons! They have abandoned the Lord; they have blasphemed the Holy One of Israel; they have turned backward in estrangement.
verses.1:5: "Where should I strike you further, as you add transgression? The whole head is faint, and the whole heart is grieving.
verses.1:6: From the sole of the foot to the crown of the head, there is no soundness in it; wound, and bruise, and swelling sore have not been bandaged, nor treated with medicine, nor soothed with oil.
verses.1:7: Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire; in your presence foreigners devour your country, and it will be laid desolate as in an enemy devastation.
verses.1:8: And the daughter of Zion will be left like a shelter in a vineyard, and like a hut in a cucumber field, and like a city that is being devastated."
verses.1:9: Unless the Lord of hosts had left us seed, we would have been like Sodom, and we would resemble Gomorrah.
verses.1:10: Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom; listen with your ears to the law of our God, people of Gomorrah.
verses.1:11: "Of what use to Me is the multitude of your sacrifices?" says the Lord. "I am full; I have not desired burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fattened animals, and the blood of calves and lambs and male goats.
verses.1:12: When you came before My sight, who sought these things from your hands, that you should walk in My courts?
verses.1:13: Do not offer sacrifice in vain anymore; incense is an abomination to Me. New moon and sabbath, and other festivals, I will not endure; your assemblies are wicked.
verses.1:14: My soul hates your new moons and your solemn festivals; they have become burdensome to Me; I have grown weary enduring them.
verses.1:15: And when you stretch out your hands, I will turn My eyes away from you, and when you multiply prayer, I will not listen, for your hands are full of blood.
verses.1:16: Wash yourselves, be clean; remove the evil of your thoughts from My eyes; cease acting perversely,
verses.1:17: learn to do good; seek justice, come to the aid of the oppressed, render justice for the orphan, defend the widow.
verses.1:18: And come, and reprove Me," says the Lord. "If your sins are like scarlet, they will be whitened like snow; and if they are red like crimson, they will be like white wool.
verses.1:19: If you are willing and listen to Me, you will eat the good things of the land.
verses.1:20: But if you refuse and provoke Me to anger, the sword will devour you, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken."
verses.1:21: How has the faithful city, full of justice, become a prostitute? Righteousness lived in her, but now murderers.
verses.1:22: Your silver has been turned into dross; your wine has been mixed with water.
verses.1:23: Your rulers are unfaithful, companions of thieves. All of them love gifts; they pursue rewards. They do not render justice for the orphan, and the case of the widow does not come before them.
verses.1:24: Because of this the Lord, the God of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, says: "Alas! I will take comfort over My adversaries, and I will be avenged on My enemies.
verses.1:25: And I will turn My hand toward you, and I will smelt away your dross to purity, and I will remove all your tin.
verses.1:26: And I will restore your judges as they were before, and your counselors as in ancient times; after these things you will be called the city of the righteous one, the faithful city."
verses.1:27: Zion will be redeemed in justice, and they will bring her back in righteousness.
verses.1:28: And He will crush the wicked and sinners together, and those who have abandoned the Lord will be consumed.
verses.1:29: For they will be put to shame because of the idols to which they sacrificed, and you will blush over the gardens that you had chosen,
verses.1:30: when you become like an oak with its leaves falling, and like a garden without water.
verses.1:31: And your strength will be like the ash of flax fibers, and your work like a spark; and both will be set on fire together, and there will be no one to extinguish it.
verses.2:1: The word that Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw regarding Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.2:2: And it will be in the last days: the mountain of the house of the Lord will be prepared on the summit of the mountains, and it will be lifted up above the hills, and all nations will flow to it,
verses.2:3: and many peoples will go and say, "Come, and let us ascend to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and He will teach us His ways, and we will walk in His paths, for the law will go out from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem."
verses.2:4: And He will judge the nations, and He will reprove many peoples; and they will forge their swords into plowshares, and their spears into sickles. Nation will not lift up a sword against nation, nor will they be trained for battle anymore.
verses.2:5: House of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.
verses.2:6: For You have cast away Your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled as in former times, and they have had diviners like the Philistines, and they have clung to foreign children.
verses.2:7: The land is filled with silver and gold, and there is no end to their treasures.
verses.2:8: And their land is filled with horses, and their chariots are innumerable. And their land is filled with idols; they have worshiped the work of their own hands, which their fingers have made.
verses.2:9: And mankind has bowed down, and man has been humbled; therefore do not forgive them.
verses.2:10: Enter into the rock, and hide yourself in the dug-out ground from the face of the fear of the Lord, and from the glory of His majesty.
verses.2:11: The lofty eyes of mankind have been humbled, and the haughtiness of men will be bowed down; but the Lord alone will be exalted in that day.
verses.2:12: For the day of the Lord of hosts is against everyone proud and high, and against everyone arrogant, and he will be humbled;
verses.2:13: and against all the lofty and towering cedars of Lebanon, and against all the oaks of Bashan,
verses.2:14: and against all the high mountains, and against all the elevated hills,
verses.2:15: and against every high tower, and against every fortified wall,
verses.2:16: and against all the ships of Tarshish, and against everything that is beautiful to see,
verses.2:17: and the loftiness of human beings will be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men will be humbled, and the Lord alone will be lifted up in that day;
verses.2:18: and the idols will be completely crushed;
verses.2:19: and they will enter into the caves of the rocks and into the chasms of the earth, from the face of the terror of the Lord and from the glory of His majesty, when He rises up to strike the earth.
verses.2:20: In that day a man will cast away the idols of his silver and the images of his gold, which he had made for himself to worship: moles and bats.
verses.2:21: And he goes into the clefts of the rocks and into the caverns of the crags, from the face of the terror of the Lord, and from the glory of His majesty, when He rises up to strike the earth.
verses.3:1: For look, the Sovereign, the Lord of hosts, will take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the sturdy and the mighty, every support of bread and every support of water;
verses.3:2: the mighty man and the fighting man, the judge and the prophet, and the diviner and the elder;
verses.3:3: the leader over fifty, and the one honorable in appearance, and the counselor, and the wise among master builders, and the discerning in mystical speech.
verses.3:4: And I will give boys as their leaders, and the effeminate will rule over them;
verses.3:5: and the people will fall upon one another, man against man, and each one against his neighbor; the boy will raise a tumult against the elder, and the ignoble against the noble.
verses.3:6: For a man will take hold of his brother, one of his father's household: "You have clothing; be our leader, and let this ruin be under your hand."
verses.3:7: He will answer on that day, saying, "I am not a physician, and in my house there is neither bread nor clothing; do not appoint me leader of the people."
verses.3:8: For Jerusalem has collapsed, and Judah has fallen, because their tongue and their doings are against the Lord, to provoke the eyes of His majesty.
verses.3:9: The expression of their face has answered them; and they have proclaimed their sin like Sodom, nor have they hidden it. Woe to their soul, for evils have been repaid to them!
verses.3:10: Say to the righteous man that it is well, for he will eat the fruit of his doings.
verses.3:11: Woe to the wicked! It is for evil, because the repayment of his hands will be done to him.
verses.3:12: Their exactors have plundered My people, and women have ruled over them. My people, those who call you blessed, they themselves deceive you and destroy the way of your steps.
verses.3:13: The Lord stands to judge, and stands to judge the peoples.
verses.3:14: The Lord will come to judgment with the elders of His people and its leaders: "For you have consumed the vineyard, and the plunder of the poor is in your house.
verses.3:15: Why do you crush My people and grind the faces of the poor?" says the Lord God of hosts.
verses.3:16: And the Lord said, "Because the daughters of Zion are lifted up and have walked with outstretched neck, and went along with winks of their eyes, and clapped, walked with their feet, and proceeded with a measured step;
verses.3:17: the Lord will make bald the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will lay bare their hair."
verses.3:18: On that day the Lord will take away the ornament of footwear,
verses.3:19: and the crescents, and the collars, and the necklaces, and the bracelets, and the turbans,
verses.3:20: and the hairpins, and the anklets, and the little chains, and the scent bottles, and the earrings,
verses.3:21: and the rings, and the gems hanging on the forehead,
verses.3:22: and the changes of clothing, and the short cloaks, and the linen garments, and the pins,
verses.3:23: and the mirrors, and the fine linens, and the headbands, and the summer veils.
verses.3:24: And instead of sweet fragrance there will be a stench, and instead of a sash, a rope, and instead of curled hair, baldness, and instead of a breast-band, sackcloth.
verses.3:25: Your most handsome men also will fall by the sword, and your mighty men in battle.
verses.3:26: And her gates will grieve and mourn, and she will sit desolate on the ground.
verses.4:1: And seven women will take hold of one man on that day, saying, "We will eat our own bread and cover ourselves with our own clothing; only let your name be called over us; take away our reproach."
verses.4:2: On that day, the shoot of the Lord will be in magnificence and glory, and the fruit of the earth will be lofty, and an exultation for those who have been saved from Israel.
verses.4:3: And it will be: everyone who has been left in Zion and who remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone who is written in life in Jerusalem.
verses.4:4: If the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and washed the blood of Jerusalem from her midst, in the spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning.
verses.4:5: And the Lord will create over every place of Mount Zion, and where He has been invoked, a cloud by day and smoke, and the brightness of a flaming fire in the night; for over all glory there will be protection.
verses.4:6: And a tabernacle will be for shade by day from the heat, and for security and a hiding place from the whirlwind and from the rain.
verses.5:1: I will sing to my beloved the song of my cousin concerning His vineyard. A vineyard was made for my beloved on a horn, the son of oil.
verses.5:2: And He hedged it in, and picked the stones out of it, and planted it as a choice vineyard; and He built a tower in the midst of it, and constructed a winepress in it; and He waited for it to produce grapes, and it produced wild grapes.
verses.5:3: Now therefore, inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge between Me and My vineyard.
verses.5:4: What is there that I ought to have done further for My vineyard, and did not do for it? Or was it that I waited for it to produce grapes, and it produced wild grapes?
verses.5:5: And now I will show you what I will do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be for plundering; I will tear down its wall, and it will be for trampling.
verses.5:6: And I will make it desolate; it will not be pruned and it will not be dug; and briers and thorns will come up, and I will command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.
verses.5:7: For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the man of Judah is His delightful shoot; and I waited for it to produce judgment, and look, iniquity; and righteousness, and look, an outcry.
verses.5:8: Woe to you who join house to house, and link field to field up to the boundary of the place! Will you alone dwell in the midst of the land?
verses.5:9: "These things are in My ears," says the Lord of hosts, "unless many houses become desolate, great and beautiful, without an inhabitant.
verses.5:10: For ten acres of vineyards will produce one small flask, and thirty measures of seed will produce three measures."
verses.5:11: Woe to you who rise up in the morning to pursue drunkenness, and to drink until evening, so that you are inflamed with wine!
verses.5:12: Harp and lyre, tambourine and flute, and wine are at your banquets; and you do not regard the work of the Lord, nor do you consider the works of His hands.
verses.5:13: Therefore My people have been led captive, because they had no knowledge, and their nobles have perished from hunger, and their multitude has become parched with thirst.
verses.5:14: Therefore hell has enlarged its soul, and has opened its mouth without any limit; and her mighty ones, and her people, and her lofty and glorious ones will go down to it.
verses.5:15: And mankind will be bowed down, and man will be humbled, and the eyes of the lofty will be cast down.
verses.5:16: And the Lord of hosts will be exalted in judgment; and the holy God will be sanctified in righteousness.
verses.5:17: And lambs will graze according to their order, and strangers will eat the desolate places that have been turned into fertility.
verses.5:18: Woe to you who drag iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as with a cart rope,
verses.5:19: who say, "Let His work hurry and come quickly, so that we may see; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, and we will know it!"
verses.5:20: Woe to you who call evil good, and good evil; setting darkness as light, and light as darkness; setting bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!
verses.5:21: Woe to you who are wise in your own eyes, and discerning before yourselves.
verses.5:22: Woe to you who are powerful for drinking wine, and mighty men for mixing drunkenness,
verses.5:23: who justify the wicked for bribes, and take away the righteousness of the righteous man from him!
verses.5:24: Because of this, just as a tongue of fire devours stubble and the heat of the flame burns it up, so their root will be like ashes, and their shoot will rise like dust; for they have cast away the law of the Lord of hosts, and have blasphemed the speech of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.5:25: Therefore the fury of the Lord grew angry against His people, and He stretched out His hand over them and struck them; and the mountains were shaken, and their corpses became like dung in the middle of the streets. In all these things His fury has not turned away, but His hand is still stretched out.
verses.5:26: And He will lift up a standard among the nations far away, and He will whistle to it from the ends of the earth; and look, in haste it will come swiftly.
verses.5:27: There is none fainting nor growing weary in it; it will neither slumber nor sleep, neither will the belt of its loins be loosened, nor will the strap of its sandal be broken.
verses.5:28: Its arrows are sharp, and all its bows are drawn. The hooves of its horses are like flint, and its wheels are like the rush of a tempest.
verses.5:29: Its roar is like a lion's; it will roar like young lions; and it will snarl, and grasp the prey, and embrace it, and there will be no one to rescue.
verses.5:30: And it will resound over them on that day like the sound of the sea; we will look upon the land, and look, darkness of distress, and the light has been darkened in its gloom.
verses.6:1: In the year in which King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a high and uplifted throne, and the things that were beneath Him were filling the temple.
verses.6:2: Seraphim stood above it: one had six wings, and another had six wings; with two they veiled His face, and with two they veiled His feet, and with two they flew.
verses.6:3: And they called out one to another and said, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord, God of hosts; all the earth is full of His glory."
verses.6:4: And the lintels of the hinges were shaken by the voice of the one calling out, and the house was filled with smoke.
verses.6:5: And I said, "Woe to me, because I have kept silent, because I am a man with polluted lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people having polluted lips, and I have seen the King, the Lord of hosts, with my eyes."
verses.6:6: And one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a small stone, which he had taken from the altar with tongs,
verses.6:7: and he touched my mouth and said, "Look, this has touched your lips, and your iniquity will be taken away, and your sin will be cleansed."
verses.6:8: And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send? And who will go for Us?" And I said, "Here I am; send me."
verses.6:9: And He said, "Go, and you will say to this people, 'Hear, you who hear, and do not understand; and see a vision, and do not know.'
verses.6:10: Blind the heart of this people, and make its ears heavy, and shut its eyes, so that it may not perhaps see with its eyes, and hear with its ears, and understand with its heart, and be converted, and I heal it."
verses.6:11: And I said, "How long, Lord?" And He said, "Until the cities are made desolate without an inhabitant, and the houses without a man, and the land will be left deserted.
verses.6:12: And the Lord will remove men far away, and she who had been abandoned in the midst of the land will be multiplied.
verses.6:13: And still there will be a tenth in it, and it will be converted, and it will be for a display like a terebinth, and like an oak that spreads out its branches; that which stands in it will be a holy seed."
verses.7:1: And it happened in the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to make war against it, and they were not able
verses.7:2: to conquer it. And they reported to the house of David, saying, "Syria has rested upon Ephraim." And his heart was shaken, and the heart of his people, just as the trees of the forests are moved before the face of the wind.
verses.7:3: And the Lord said to Isaiah, "Go out to meet Ahaz, you and he who is left behind, Jashub, your son, to the end of the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road of the fuller's field,
verses.7:4: and you will say to him, 'See that you keep quiet; do not fear, and do not let your heart be terrified by these two tails of smoking firebrands, at the anger of the fury of Rezin, king of Syria, and of the son of Remaliah,
verses.7:5: because Syria has entered into counsel against you for evil, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, saying,
verses.7:6: "Let us go up to Judah, and let us rouse it, and let us tear it away to ourselves, and let us set the son of Tabeel as king in its midst."
verses.7:7: This is what the Lord God says: "It will not stand, and this will not come to be;
verses.7:8: rather, the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and sixty-five years more, and Ephraim will cease to be a people;
verses.7:9: and the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not believe, you will not remain."'"
verses.7:10: And the Lord spoke further to Ahaz, saying,
verses.7:11: "Ask a sign for yourself from the Lord your God, into the depth of the underworld, or into the height above."
verses.7:12: And Ahaz said, "I will not ask, and I will not test the Lord."
verses.7:13: And he said, "Hear therefore, house of David: is it too little for you to be troublesome to men, that you are troublesome to my God as well?
verses.7:14: For this reason the Lord Himself will give you a sign: look, a virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and His name will be called Immanuel.
verses.7:15: He will eat butter and honey, so that He may know how to reject evil and choose good.
verses.7:16: For before the boy knows how to reject evil and choose good, the land that you detest will be abandoned before the face of its two kings.
verses.7:17: The Lord will bring upon you, and upon your people, and upon the house of your father, days that have not come since the days of the separation of Ephraim from Judah, with the king of the Assyrians.
verses.7:18: And it will be in that day: the Lord will whistle for the fly that is at the end of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria;
verses.7:19: and they will come, and all of them will rest in the torrents of the valleys, and in the caverns of the rocks, and in all the thickets, and in all the holes.
verses.7:20: In that day the Lord will shave with a hired razor, by those who are beyond the river, by the king of the Assyrians, the head and the hair of the feet, and the whole beard.
verses.7:21: And it will be in that day: a man will raise a cow of the herd and two sheep,
verses.7:22: and because of the abundance of milk, he will eat butter; for everyone who is left in the midst of the land will eat butter and honey.
verses.7:23: And it will be in that day: every place where there were a thousand vines, for a thousand pieces of silver, will become thorns and briers.
verses.7:24: With arrows and a bow they will enter there, for briers and thorns will be in the whole land.
verses.7:25: And as for all the mountains that will be hoed with a hoe, the terror of thorns and briers will not come there; and it will be for the pastures of the ox, and for the trampling of the flock."
verses.8:1: And the Lord said to me, "Take for yourself a large book, and write in it with a man's stylus, 'Swiftly strip the spoils, quickly plunder.'"
verses.8:2: And I summoned for myself faithful witnesses: Uriah the priest, and Zechariah, son of Berechiah;
verses.8:3: and I approached the prophetess, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. And the Lord said to me, "Call his name, 'Hasten to strip the spoils; hurry to plunder,'
verses.8:4: for before the boy knows how to call his father and his mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria will be taken away before the king of the Assyrians."
verses.8:5: And the Lord spoke to me yet again, saying,
verses.8:6: "Because this people has rejected the waters of Shiloah, which flow in silence, and has rather adopted Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
verses.8:7: for this reason, look, the Lord will bring upon them the strong and many waters of the river, the king of the Assyrians and all his glory; and it will rise above all its channels, and it will flow over all its banks;
verses.8:8: and it will go through Judah, overflowing and passing on; it will come up to the neck. And the outstretching of its wings will fill the breadth of Your land, Immanuel!"
verses.8:9: Gather together, peoples, and be conquered; and listen, all distant lands: be strengthened, and be conquered; gird yourselves, and be conquered.
verses.8:10: Enter into counsel, and it will be shattered; speak a word, and it will not happen, because God is with us.
verses.8:11: For this is what the Lord said to me: as with a strong hand He instructed me, so that I would not go in the way of this people, saying,
verses.8:12: "Do not say, 'Conspiracy,' for everything that this people speaks is a conspiracy; and do not fear its fear, nor be in dread.
verses.8:13: Sanctify the Lord of hosts Himself; let Him be your dread, and let Him be your terror;
verses.8:14: and He will be a sanctification for you, yet a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense for the two houses of Israel, a snare and a ruin for those who dwell in Jerusalem.
verses.8:15: And very many of them will stumble, and fall, and be crushed, and be ensnared, and be captured."
verses.8:16: Bind up the testimony; seal the law among my disciples.
verses.8:17: And I will wait for the Lord, who hides His face from the house of Jacob, and I will await Him.
verses.8:18: Look, I and my children, whom the Lord has given to me, are for a sign and for a portent to Israel from the Lord of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
verses.8:19: And when they say to you, "Inquire of mediums and of diviners who chirp in their incantations," should not a people inquire of its God? On behalf of the living, from the dead?
verses.8:20: To the law rather, and to the testimony. But if they do not speak according to this word, there will be no morning light for them.
verses.8:21: And he will pass through it, collapse, and grow hungry; and when he is hungry, he will grow angry. And he will curse his king and his God, and he will look upward,
verses.8:22: and he will gaze at the earth; and look: tribulation and darkness, dissolution and anguish, and pursuing gloom, and he will not be able to fly away from his anguish.
verses.8:23: At the first time the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali was lightened, and at the last the way of the sea beyond the Jordan, of Galilee of the nations, was weighed down.
verses.9:1: The people who were walking in darkness have seen a great light; for those living in the region of the shadow of death, light has risen upon them.
verses.9:2: You have multiplied the nation, and have not magnified the joy. They will rejoice before You, like those who rejoice at the harvest, as victors exult after plunder has been taken, when they divide the spoils.
verses.9:3: For You have overcome the yoke of its burden, and the rod of its shoulder, and the scepter of its taskmaster, as in the day of Midian.
verses.9:4: For every plundering by violence with tumult, and a garment mixed with blood, will be for burning, and food for fire.
verses.9:5: For a little child has been born to us, and a son has been given to us, and sovereignty has come upon His shoulder; and His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, God, Mighty, Father of the Age to Come, Prince of Peace.
verses.9:6: His dominion will be multiplied, and of peace there will be no end; He will sit upon the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and strengthen it in judgment and righteousness, from now on and forever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this.
verses.9:7: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it fell upon Israel.
verses.9:8: And all the people of Ephraim will know, and the inhabitants of Samaria, saying in pride and greatness of heart:
verses.9:9: "The bricks have fallen, but we will build with squared stones; they have cut down the sycamores, but we will substitute cedars."
verses.9:10: And the Lord will raise up the adversaries of Rezin over him, and will turn his enemies into tumult:
verses.9:11: Syria from the east, and the Philistines from the west; and they will devour Israel with a full mouth. In all these things His fury has not been turned away, but His hand is still stretched out.
verses.9:12: And the people have not returned to the One striking them, and they have not sought the Lord of hosts.
verses.9:13: And the Lord will destroy from Israel head and tail, the one bowing down and the one restraining, in one day.
verses.9:14: The aged and honorable man, he is the head; and the prophet teaching falsehood, he is the tail.
verses.9:15: And those who call this people blessed will be deceivers, and those who are called blessed will be thrown headlong.
verses.9:16: Because of this the Lord will not rejoice over its young men, and He will not have mercy on its orphans and widows; for everyone is a hypocrite and wicked, and every mouth has spoken folly. In all these things His fury has not been turned away, but His hand is still stretched out.
verses.9:17: For ungodliness has been kindled like fire; it will devour the brier and the thorn, and will be kindled in the thickness of the forest, and the pride of smoke will roll upward.
verses.9:18: In the anger of the Lord of hosts the land has been thrown into turmoil, and the people will be like food for fire; a man will not spare his own brother.
verses.9:19: And he will turn aside to the right, and will be hungry; and he will eat on the left, and will not be satisfied; each one will devour the flesh of his own arm: Manasseh will devour Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they themselves are against Judah.
verses.9:20: In all these things His fury has not been turned away, but His hand is still stretched out.
verses.10:1: Woe to those who enact unjust laws, and who, writing, have written unrighteousness,
verses.10:2: to oppress the poor in judgment and do violence to the cause of the humble of My people, so that widows might be their plunder and they might rob the orphans.
verses.10:3: What will you do in the day of visitation, and of calamity coming from afar? To whose help will you flee for refuge? And where will you leave your glory,
verses.10:4: so that you may not be bowed down under a bond, and fall with those who are killed? Over all these things His fury has not been turned away, but His hand is still stretched out.
verses.10:5: Woe to Assyria! He himself is the rod of My fury and the staff; in their hand is My indignation.
verses.10:6: To a deceitful nation I will send him, and against the people of My fury I will command him, to carry off spoils and seize plunder, and to place it for trampling like the mud of the streets.
verses.10:7: Yet he himself will not think so, and his heart will not reckon it this way; rather, his heart will be for crushing and for the extermination of not a few nations.
verses.10:9: "Are not my princes altogether kings? As Carchemish is, is not Calno also? And as Arpad is, is not Hamath? As Damascus is, is not Samaria?
verses.10:10: Just as my hand has found the kingdoms of the idol, so also their images from Jerusalem and from Samaria.
verses.10:11: Just as I have done to Samaria and to its idols, will I not also do to Jerusalem and to its images?"
verses.10:12: And it will come to pass, when the Lord has fulfilled all His works on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the arrogant heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of the loftiness of his eyes.
verses.10:13: For he has said: "In the strength of my hand I have acted, and in my wisdom I have understood; and I have removed the boundaries of the peoples, and have plundered their princes, and like a mighty one I have pulled down those seated on high.
verses.10:14: And my hand has found the strength of the peoples like a nest; and just as eggs that have been abandoned are gathered, so I myself have gathered the whole earth; and there was none who moved a wing, or opened a mouth, or chirped."
verses.10:15: Will the axe boast against the one who cuts with it? Or will the saw exalt itself against the one by whom it is drawn? It is as if a rod were to raise itself against the one raising it, and a staff were to exalt itself, which is indeed wood.
verses.10:16: Because of this, the Sovereign, the Lord of hosts, will send leanness among his fat ones; and beneath his glory, once kindled, it will burn like the burning of fire.
verses.10:17: And the light of Israel will be in fire, and its Holy One in flame; and his thorn and brier will be kindled and devoured in one day.
verses.10:18: And the glory of his forest and of his fruitful field will be consumed from soul even to flesh; and he will be a fugitive in terror.
verses.10:19: And the remnant of the trees of his forest will be numbered because of their fewness, and a boy will write them down.
verses.10:20: And it will come to pass in that day: the remainder of Israel, and those who have fled from the house of Jacob, will no longer lean upon the one who strikes them, but will lean upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
verses.10:21: A remnant will return; the remnant, I say, of Jacob, to the mighty God.
verses.10:22: For even if your people, Israel, are like the sand of the sea, a remnant will return from it; a shortened completion will overflow with righteousness.
verses.10:23: For the Lord God of hosts will bring about a completion and a shortening in the midst of all the earth.
verses.10:24: Because of this, this is what the Lord God of hosts says: "Do not be afraid of Assyria, My people, dweller in Zion: he will strike you with a rod, and will lift up his staff over you, in the way of Egypt.
verses.10:25: For yet a little, a very brief while, and the indignation and My fury will be completed upon their wickedness."
verses.10:26: And the Lord of hosts will raise up a scourge against him, according to the blow against Midian at the rock of Oreb; and His rod will be over the sea, and He will lift it up in the way of Egypt.
verses.10:27: And it will come to pass in that day: his burden will be taken away from your shoulder and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke will rot away before the face of the oil.
verses.10:28: He will come to Aiath, he will pass through Migron, at Michmash he will deposit his baggage.
verses.10:29: They have passed over in haste: "Geba is our lodging." Ramah has been stunned; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
verses.10:30: Neigh with your voice, daughter of Gallim; pay attention, Laishah; poor little Anathoth!
verses.10:31: Madmenah has departed; inhabitants of Gebim, take courage!
verses.10:32: There is still a day to halt at Nob; he will shake his hand against the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
verses.10:33: Look, the Sovereign, the Lord of hosts, will shatter the small flask in terror; and those lofty in stature will be cut down, and the exalted will be humbled.
verses.10:34: And the thickets of the forest will be overturned with iron; and Lebanon will fall along with the lofty ones.
verses.11:1: And a shoot will go forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will rise from his root.
verses.11:2: And the Spirit of the Lord will rest upon Him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of knowledge and piety,
verses.11:3: and the spirit of the fear of the Lord will fill Him. He will not judge according to the sight of the eyes, nor will He reprove according to the hearing of the ears;
verses.11:4: but He will judge the poor in righteousness, and will reprove in equity on behalf of the meek of the earth; and He will strike the earth with the rod of His mouth, and with the breath of His lips He will kill the wicked one.
verses.11:5: And righteousness will be the belt of His loins, and faithfulness the sash of His waist.
verses.11:6: The wolf will dwell with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; the calf, and the lion, and the sheep will stay together, and a little boy will lead them.
verses.11:7: The calf and the bear will graze; their young will rest together; and the lion will eat straw like the ox.
verses.11:8: And the nursing infant will delight itself over the hole of the asp; and the one who has been weaned will put his hand into the den of the basilisk.
verses.11:9: They will not harm, and they will not kill, in all My holy mountain, for the earth has been filled with the knowledge of the Lord, like the covering waters of the sea.
verses.11:10: In that day the root of Jesse, who stands as a sign for the peoples: Him the nations will implore, and His tomb will be glorious.
verses.11:11: And it will come to pass in that day: the Lord will extend His hand a second time to take possession of the remainder of His people, which will be left from the Assyrians, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Ethiopia, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
verses.11:12: And He will lift up a sign to the nations, and will gather the fugitives of Israel, and will assemble the dispersed of Judah from the four quarters of the earth.
verses.11:13: And the jealousy of Ephraim will be taken away, and the adversaries of Judah will perish; Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not fight against Ephraim.
verses.11:14: And they will fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines by the sea; together they will plunder the sons of the east; Idumea and Moab will be at the command of their hand, and the sons of Ammon will be obedient.
verses.11:15: And the Lord will lay waste the tongue of the sea of Egypt, and He will lift up His hand over the river in the strength of His Spirit; and He will strike it into seven streams, so that they may cross through it with shoes on.
verses.11:16: And there will be a way for My remaining people who will be left from the Assyrians, just as there was for Israel in that day when they went up from the land of Egypt.
verses.12:1: And you will say on that day: "I will give thanks to You, Lord, because You were angry with me; Your fury has turned back, and You have comforted me.
verses.12:2: Look, God is my Savior; I will act confidently and I will not be afraid, because the Lord is my strength and my praise, and He has become salvation to me."
verses.12:3: You will draw waters with joy from the springs of the Savior.
verses.12:4: And you will say on that day: "Give thanks to the Lord and call upon His name; make His works known among the peoples; remember that His name is exalted.
verses.12:5: Sing to the Lord, because He has acted magnificently; declare this throughout the whole earth.
verses.12:6: Exult and praise, dwelling of Zion, because the Holy One of Israel is great in your midst."
verses.13:1: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah, the son of Amoz, saw.
verses.13:2: Upon a dark mountain lift up a banner; raise the voice, lift up the hand, and let the leaders enter the gates.
verses.13:3: I have commanded My sanctified ones, and I have summoned My mighty ones in My wrath, exulting in My glory.
verses.13:4: The sound of a multitude in the mountains, like that of thronging peoples; the sound of the roar of kings, of gathered nations. The Lord of hosts has commanded the army of war,
verses.13:5: those coming from a distant land, from the extremity of heaven; the Lord and the vessels of His fury, so that He may destroy the whole earth.
verses.13:6: Wail, because the day of the Lord is near; it will come like devastation from the Lord.
verses.13:7: Because of this all hands will go limp, and every human heart will waste away,
verses.13:8: and be crushed. Pangs and pains will take hold; they will be in pain like a woman in labor; each one will be stunned at his neighbor; their expressions will be scorched faces.
verses.13:9: Look, the day of the Lord will come, cruel and full of indignation, and of wrath and fury, to make the earth a desolation and to crush its sinners out of it.
verses.13:10: For the stars of heaven and their brightness will not spread out their light; the sun has been darkened at its rising, and the moon will not shine in its light.
verses.13:11: And I will punish the evils of the world, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will make the pride of the unfaithful cease, and I will humble the arrogance of the mighty.
verses.13:12: A man will be more precious than gold, and a human being than pure refined gold.
verses.13:13: For this reason I will throw heaven into turmoil, and the earth will be moved from its place, because of the indignation of the Lord of hosts, and because of the day of the wrath of His fury.
verses.13:14: And it will be like a fleeing doe, and like a sheep, and there will be no one to gather it. Each one will turn back to his own people, and they will each flee to their own land.
verses.13:15: Everyone who is found will be killed, and everyone who comes up will fall by the sword;
verses.13:16: their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses will be plundered, and their wives will be violated.
verses.13:17: Look, I will rouse the Medes against them, who do not seek silver, nor desire gold;
verses.13:18: but with arrows they will kill the little ones, and they will have no mercy on nursing wombs, and their eye will not spare the children.
verses.13:19: And that Babylon, glorious among kingdoms, the renowned pride of the Chaldeans, will be just as when the Lord overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
verses.13:20: It will not be inhabited even to the end, and it will not be founded even to generation and generation; nor will the Arab pitch tents there, nor will shepherds rest there.
verses.13:21: Instead, wild beasts will rest there, and their houses will be filled with dragons, and ostriches will dwell there, and hairy creatures will dance there;
verses.13:22: and owls will answer there in its halls, and sirens in the temples of pleasure.
verses.14:1: Its time is near to come, and its days will not be prolonged. For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and He will still choose from Israel, and He will make them rest upon their own ground; the stranger will be joined to them and will cling to the house of Jacob.
verses.14:2: And peoples will take them and bring them to their own place; and the house of Israel will possess them upon the land of the Lord as servants and maidservants; and they will be taking captive those who had taken them captive, and they will subdue their oppressors.
verses.14:3: And it will be on that day, when God gives you rest from your toil, and from your turmoil, and from the harsh servitude in which you previously served,
verses.14:4: you will take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and you will say: "How has the oppressor ceased; how has tribute come to rest?
verses.14:5: The Lord has shattered the staff of the wicked, the rod of the rulers,
verses.14:6: striking the peoples in indignation with an incurable blow, subduing the nations in fury, persecuting cruelly.
verses.14:7: The whole earth has come to rest and grown silent; it has rejoiced and exulted;
verses.14:8: the fir trees also have been glad over you, and the cedars of Lebanon: 'Since you fell asleep, no one will come up to cut us down.'
verses.14:9: The underworld below has been thrown into turmoil to meet your coming; it has roused the giants for you. All the princes of the earth have risen from their thrones, all the princes of the nations.
verses.14:10: All of them will answer and say to you: 'You too have been wounded just like us; you have become like us.'
verses.14:11: Your pride has been dragged down to the underworld, your corpse has fallen; beneath you the moth will be spread out, and worms will be your covering.
verses.14:12: How have you fallen from heaven, Lucifer, who rose in the morning? Have you crashed down to the earth, you who wounded the nations?
verses.14:13: You who said in your heart: 'I will ascend into heaven, above the stars of God I will exalt my throne; I will sit on the mountain of the covenant, on the sides of the north;
verses.14:14: I will ascend above the height of the clouds, I will be like the Most High'?
verses.14:15: Yet you will be dragged down to the underworld, into the depth of the pit.
verses.14:16: Those who see you will lean toward you and look closely at you: 'Is this really the man who threw the earth into turmoil, who shook kingdoms,
verses.14:17: who made the world a desert and destroyed its cities, who did not open the prison for his captives?'
verses.14:18: All the kings of the nations, every one of them, have slept in glory, each man in his own house;
verses.14:19: but you have been cast out from your tomb like a useless shoot, defiled and wrapped up with those who were killed by the sword and went down to the foundations of the pit, like a rotting corpse.
verses.14:20: You will not have fellowship, not even with them in burial; for you have destroyed your own land, you have killed your own people; the offspring of the most wicked will not be named forever.
verses.14:21: Prepare his sons for slaughter because of the iniquity of their fathers; they will not rise up, nor inherit the earth, nor fill the face of the world with cities."
verses.14:22: "And I will rise up against them," says the Lord of hosts, "and I will destroy the name of Babylon, and the remnant, and shoot, and posterity," says the Lord,
verses.14:23: "and I will turn it into a possession of the hedgehog, and into marshes of waters, and I will sweep it with a broom, grinding it down," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.14:24: The Lord of hosts has sworn, saying: "Surely, just as I have thought, so it will be; and as I have considered in mind,
verses.14:25: so it will come about: that I will crush the Assyrian in My land, and on My mountains I will trample him; and his yoke will be taken away from them, and his burden will be lifted from their shoulder.
verses.14:26: This is the plan that I have devised over the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations."
verses.14:27: For the Lord of hosts has decreed, and who will be able to nullify it? And His hand is stretched out, and who will turn it back?
verses.14:28: In the year in which King Ahaz died, this burden came:
verses.14:29: Do not rejoice, all of you, Philistia, because the rod of the one who struck you has been broken to pieces; for from the root of the serpent a basilisk will come out, and its offspring will swallow up the bird.
verses.14:30: And the firstborn of the poor will feed, and the poor will rest confidently; and I will make your root perish in famine, and I will kill your remnant.
verses.14:31: Wail, gate; cry out, city; all Philistia has been laid prostrate; for smoke will come from the north, and there is no one who will escape its column.
verses.14:32: And what will be answered to the messengers of the nation? That the Lord has founded Zion, and in Him the poor of His people will hope.
verses.15:1: The burden of Moab. Because by night Ar of Moab was laid waste, it fell silent; because by night the wall of Moab was laid waste, it fell silent.
verses.15:2: The house went up, and Dibon to the high places, for mourning over Nebo; and over Medeba, Moab wailed; on all its heads is baldness, and every beard will be shaved.
verses.15:3: In its crossroads they are girded with sackcloth; on its rooftops and in its squares all wailing goes down into weeping.
verses.15:4: Heshbon and Elealeh will cry out, as far as Jahaz their voice has been heard; over this the armed men of Moab will wail, its soul will wail to itself.
verses.15:5: My heart will cry out for Moab; its bars reach as far as Zoar, a three-year-old heifer; for by the ascent of Luhith it will go up weeping, and on the road of Horonaim they will raise a cry of destruction.
verses.15:6: For the waters of Nimrim will be desolate, because the grass has dried up, the shoot has failed, all greenery has perished.
verses.15:7: According to the greatness of the work, so also is their visitation: they will lead them to the brook of the Willows.
verses.15:8: For the cry has gone around the border of Moab; as far as Gallim is its wailing, and as far as the well of Elim is its cry.
verses.15:9: For the waters of Dibon are filled with blood; for I will set additions upon Dibon: a lion for those who flee from Moab, and for the remnant of the land.
verses.16:1: Send forth the lamb, Lord, the ruler of the earth, from the rock of the desert to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
verses.16:2: And it will be: like a fleeing bird and young birds flying away from the nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the crossing of Arnon.
verses.16:3: Take counsel, convene a council; make your shadow like night at midday; hide those who flee, and do not betray the wanderers.
verses.16:4: My fugitives will dwell with you; Moab, be their hiding place from the face of the destroyer: for the dust has come to an end, the wretched one has been consumed, he who trampled the earth has ceased.
verses.16:5: And a throne will be prepared in mercy, and one will sit upon it in truth in the tent of David, judging and seeking justice, and swiftly rendering what is just.
verses.16:6: We have heard of the pride of Moab: it is exceedingly proud; its pride, and its arrogance, and its indignation are greater than its strength.
verses.16:7: Therefore Moab will wail for Moab; all of it will wail: to those who rejoice over the walls of baked brick, speak of their wounds.
verses.16:8: For the outskirts of Heshbon are desolate, and the lords of the nations have cut down the vine of Sibmah: its shoots reached as far as Jazer, they wandered in the desert; its branches were abandoned, they crossed the sea.
verses.16:9: Over this I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah; I will drench you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, for the voice of the treaders has rushed upon your vintage and upon your harvest.
verses.16:10: And gladness and exultation will be taken away from Carmel, and in the vineyards no one will exult or shout for joy. The one who was accustomed to tread will not tread wine in the winepress; I have taken away the voice of the treaders.
verses.16:11: Over this my belly will sound like a harp for Moab, and my inward parts for the wall of baked brick.
verses.16:12: And it will be: when it appears that Moab has labored upon its high places, it will enter its sanctuary to plead, and it will not prevail.
verses.16:13: This is the word that the Lord spoke to Moab from that time.
verses.16:14: And now the Lord has spoken, saying, "In three years, like the years of a hired worker, the glory of Moab over all the numerous people will be taken away, and it will be left small and meager, by no means numerous."
verses.17:1: The burden of Damascus. "Look, Damascus will cease to be a city, and it will be like a heap of stones in ruin.
verses.17:2: The abandoned cities of Aroer will be for flocks, and they will rest there, and there will be no one to frighten them.
verses.17:3: And help will cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus; and the remnant of Syria will be like the glory of the sons of Israel," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.17:4: "And it will be in that day: the glory of Jacob will be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh will waste away.
verses.17:5: And it will be like one gathering what remains in the harvest, and his arm will collect the ears of grain; and it will be like one seeking ears of grain in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.17:6: And there will be left in it like a cluster of grapes and like the shaking of an olive tree, two or three olives at the top of a branch, or four or five on its topmost branches, its fruit," says the Lord God of Israel.
verses.17:7: In that day man will bow down to his Maker, and his eyes will look to the Holy One of Israel;
verses.17:8: and he will not bow down to the altars that his hands made; and he will not look to what his fingers fashioned, the groves and the shrines.
verses.17:9: In that day the cities of its strength will be abandoned like plows and grainfields that were abandoned before the face of the sons of Israel; and you will be desolate.
verses.17:10: Because you have forgotten God your Savior, and have not remembered your strong Helper: therefore you will plant a faithful planting, and you will sow a foreign shoot;
verses.17:11: on the day of your planting there will be a wild vine, and in the morning your seed will blossom; the harvest has been taken away on the day of inheritance, and one will grieve severely.
verses.17:12: Woe to the multitude of many peoples, like the multitude of the roaring sea; and the tumult of crowds, like the roar of many waters.
verses.17:13: The peoples will roar like the roar of overflowing waters, and He will rebuke it, and it will flee far away; and it will be swept away like the dust of the mountains before the face of the wind, and like a whirlwind before a storm.
verses.17:14: At the time of evening, and look, turmoil; in the morning, and it will not remain. This is the portion of those who laid us waste, and the lot of those who plunder us.
verses.18:1: Woe to the land, the cymbal of wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,
verses.18:2: which sends envoys by sea, and in vessels of papyrus upon the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a nation uprooted and torn to pieces, to a terrifying people, after whom there is no other, to a nation waiting and trampled down, whose land the rivers have plundered.
verses.18:3: All you inhabitants of the world, who dwell on the earth, when a standard is lifted up on the mountains, you will see, and you will hear the blast of the trumpet.
verses.18:4: For this is what the Lord says to me: "I will be still and look on in My place, as the midday light is clear, and as a cloud of dew in the day of harvest."
verses.18:5: For before the harvest it has blossomed completely, and unripe perfection will sprout; and its shoots will be cut off with pruning hooks, and whatever has been left behind will be severed and shaken off.
verses.18:6: And they will be left together to the birds of the mountains and to the beasts of the earth; and in perpetual summer the birds will be upon it, and all the beasts of the earth will spend the winter upon it.
verses.18:7: At that time a gift will be brought to the Lord of hosts from a people pulled apart and torn to pieces, from a terrifying people, after whom there has been no other, from a nation waiting, waiting and trampled down, whose land the rivers have plundered, to the place of the name of the Lord of hosts, Mount Zion.
verses.19:1: The burden of Egypt. Look, the Lord will ascend upon a light cloud and will enter Egypt, and the idols of Egypt will be shaken at His presence, and the heart of Egypt will melt in its midst.
verses.19:2: "And I will cause the Egyptians to clash against the Egyptians; and a man will fight against his brother, and a man against his friend, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
verses.19:3: And the spirit of Egypt will be shattered within its inward parts, and I will cast down its counsel; and they will consult their idols, and their diviners, and mediums, and soothsayers.
verses.19:4: And I will hand Egypt over into the hand of cruel masters, and a strong king will rule over them," says the Lord God of hosts.
verses.19:5: And the water from the sea will dry up, and the river will become desolate and parched.
verses.19:6: And the rivers will fail; the streams of the embankments will dwindle and dry up; the reed and the rush will wither.
verses.19:7: The bed of the stream will be laid bare from its source, and every irrigated sowing will dry up, wither, and be no more.
verses.19:8: And the fishermen will grieve, and all who cast a hook into the river will mourn; and those who spread a net over the surface of the waters will languish.
verses.19:9: Those who worked flax will be put to shame, combing and weaving fine fabrics.
verses.19:10: And its irrigated grounds will droop: all who made ponds to catch fish.
verses.19:11: Foolish are the princes of Tanis; the wise counselors of Pharaoh have given unwise counsel. How will you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of wise men, a son of ancient kings"?
verses.19:12: Where are your wise men now? Let them announce to you and declare what the Lord of hosts has planned against Egypt.
verses.19:13: The princes of Tanis have become foolish; the princes of Memphis have languished; they have deceived Egypt, the cornerstone of its peoples.
verses.19:14: The Lord has mixed a spirit of dizziness in its midst; and they have made Egypt stagger in all its work, just as a drunken and vomiting man staggers.
verses.19:15: And there will be no work for Egypt that can make head and tail, the one bending down and the one restraining.
verses.19:16: In that day Egypt will be like women; and they will be stunned and will fear at the shaking of the hand of the Lord of hosts, which He Himself will shake over it.
verses.19:17: And the land of Judah will be a terror to Egypt; everyone who remembers it will be terrified because of the counsel of the Lord of hosts, which He Himself has planned against it.
verses.19:18: In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt speaking the language of Canaan and swearing by the Lord of hosts; one will be called "City of the Sun."
verses.19:19: In that day there will be an altar of the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a monument of the Lord beside its border.
verses.19:20: It will be for a sign and a witness to the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt; for they will cry out to the Lord because of distress, and He will send them a savior and a defender who will deliver them.
verses.19:21: And the Lord will be known by Egypt, and the Egyptians will know the Lord in that day; and they will worship Him with sacrifices and with gifts; and they will vow vows to the Lord and fulfill them.
verses.19:22: And the Lord will strike Egypt with a plague, and He will heal it; and they will return to the Lord, and He will be appeased toward them, and He will heal them.
verses.19:23: In that day there will be a road from Egypt to Assyria; and the Assyrian will go into Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria, and the Egyptians will serve Assyria.
verses.19:24: In that day Israel will be a third with the Egyptian and the Assyrian, a blessing in the midst of the earth,
verses.19:25: which the Lord of hosts has blessed, saying, "Blessed be My people of Egypt, and the work of My hands for the Assyrian, while My inheritance is Israel."
verses.20:1: In the year in which Thathan entered Ashdod, when Sargon, king of the Assyrians, had sent him, and had fought against Ashdod and captured it,
verses.20:2: at that time the Lord spoke by the hand of Isaiah, son of Amoz, saying, "Go, and untie the sackcloth from your loins, and remove your sandals from your feet." And he did so, going naked and barefoot.
verses.20:3: And the Lord said, "Just as My servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot, he will be a sign and a wonder of three years against Egypt and against Ethiopia;
verses.20:4: so the king of the Assyrians will drive the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, with buttocks uncovered, to the disgrace of Egypt."
verses.20:5: And they will fear and be put to shame because of Ethiopia, their hope, and because of Egypt, their glory.
verses.20:6: And the inhabitant of this island will say in that day, "Look, this was our hope, to whom we fled for help, that they might deliver us from the presence of the king of the Assyrians; and how will we ourselves be able to escape?"
verses.21:1: The burden of the desert of the sea. Just as whirlwinds come from the southwest, it comes from the desert, from a terrifying land.
verses.21:2: A harsh vision has been announced to me: he who is unbelieving acts unfaithfully, and he who is a ravager lays waste. "Go up, Elam; lay siege, Mede; I have made all its groaning cease."
verses.21:3: Therefore my loins are filled with pain; anguish has taken possession of me like the anguish of a woman in labor; I collapsed when I heard; I was thrown into turmoil when I saw.
verses.21:4: My heart has withered; darkness has stunned me; Babylon, my beloved, has been turned into a wonder for me.
verses.21:5: Set the table; watch in the watchtower those who are eating and drinking: rise up, princes, seize the shield!
verses.21:6: For the Lord said this to me: "Go and set a watchman, and whatever he sees, let him announce it."
verses.21:7: And he saw a chariot of two horsemen, a rider on a donkey, and a rider on a camel; and he watched diligently with intense gaze.
verses.21:8: And a lion cried out: "On the watchtower of the Lord I am, standing continually by day, and on my watch I am, standing all through the nights.
verses.21:9: Look, this man is coming, a rider of a two-horse chariot of horsemen!" And he answered and said: "She has fallen, Babylon has fallen, and all the carved images of her gods have been crushed to the ground."
verses.21:10: My threshing and sons of my threshing floor, what I have heard from the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, I have announced to you.
verses.21:11: The burden of Dumah. One calls out to me from Seir: "Watchman, what about the night? Watchman, what about the night?"
verses.21:12: The watchman said: "Morning comes, and night; if you inquire, inquire; turn back, come."
verses.21:13: The burden in Arabia. In the forest at evening you will sleep, on the paths of the Dedanites.
verses.21:14: Going out to meet the thirsty one, bring water, you who inhabit the land of the south; with loaves of bread, go out to meet the one who flees.
verses.21:15: For they have fled from before swords, from before a threatening sword, from before a stretched bow, from before a heavy battle.
verses.21:16: For the Lord says this to me: "Within one more year, as in the year of a hired worker, all the glory of Kedar will be taken away,
verses.21:17: and the remainder of the number of mighty archers from the sons of Kedar will be diminished," for the Lord God of Israel has spoken.
verses.22:1: The burden of the Valley of Vision. What is the matter with you also, that you too have all gone up onto the rooftops?
verses.22:2: Full of clamor, crowded city, exulting city: those of you who were killed were not killed by the sword, nor did they die in war.
verses.22:3: All your princes fled together and were harshly bound; all who were found were fettered together; they fled far away.
verses.22:4: Therefore I said: "Withdraw from me; I will weep bitterly; do not insist on comforting me over the devastation of the daughter of my people,
verses.22:5: for it is a day of slaughter, and of trampling, and of weeping, from the Lord God of hosts, in the Valley of Vision, searching the wall and magnificent upon the mountain."
verses.22:6: And Elam took up the quiver, the chariot of a mounted man, and the shield laid bare the wall.
verses.22:7: And your choicest valleys will be full of chariots, and horsemen will set their stations at the gate.
verses.22:8: And the covering of Judah will be uncovered, and on that day you will see the armory of the house of the forest.
verses.22:9: And you will see the breaches of the city of David, that they have multiplied; and you gathered the waters of the lower pool,
verses.22:10: and you counted the houses of Jerusalem, and you tore down houses to fortify the wall.
verses.22:11: And you made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool; and you did not look up to Him who had made it, and you did not see its Maker from afar.
verses.22:12: And on that day the Lord God of hosts will call to weeping, and to mourning, to baldness, and to a belt of sackcloth;
verses.22:13: and look, joy and gladness, killing calves and slaughtering rams, eating meat and drinking wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die."
verses.22:14: And the voice of the Lord of hosts was revealed in my ears: "Certainly this iniquity will not be forgiven you until you die," says the Lord God of hosts.
verses.22:15: The Lord God of hosts says this: "Go, enter to him who dwells in the tabernacle, to Shebna, the overseer of the temple, and you will say to him:
verses.22:16: 'What do you have here, or as who are you here? For you have carved out a tomb for yourself here; you have diligently carved out a monument on high, a tabernacle for yourself in the rock.
verses.22:17: Look, the Lord will cause you to be carried away, just as a rooster is carried away; and like a cloak, so He will lift you up.
verses.22:18: He will crown you with crowns, with tribulation; like a ball He will throw you into a wide and spacious land; there you will die, and there will be the chariot of your glory, the disgrace of the house of your master.
verses.22:19: And I will drive you out from your station, and from your office I will depose you.
verses.22:20: And it will be on that day: I will call My servant Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah,
verses.22:21: and I will clothe him with your tunic, and with your belt I will strengthen him, and I will give your authority into his hand; and he will be like a father to those who inhabit Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
verses.22:22: And I will place the key of the house of David upon his shoulder; and he will open, and there will be no one to shut; and he will shut, and there will be no one to open.
verses.22:23: And I will fasten him as a peg in a trustworthy place, and he will become a throne of glory for the house of his father.
verses.22:24: And they will hang upon him all the glory of the house of his father: various kinds of vessels, every small vessel, from the vessels of bowls to every vessel of musicians.'"
verses.22:25: "On that day," says the Lord of hosts, "the peg that had been fastened in a trustworthy place will be taken away, and it will be broken, and it will fall, and what had hung upon it will perish," for the Lord has spoken.
verses.23:1: The burden of Tyre. Wail, ships of the sea, for the house from which they used to come has been laid waste; from the land of Kittim it has been revealed to them.
verses.23:2: Be silent, you who dwell on the island; the merchants of Sidon, crossing over the sea, have filled you.
verses.23:3: On many waters was the seed of the Nile; the harvest of the river was her produce, and she became the trade of the nations.
verses.23:4: Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea speaks, the stronghold of the sea, saying: "I have not been in labor, and I have not given birth, and I have not reared young men, nor have I brought virgins to maturity."
verses.23:5: When it is heard in Egypt, they will grieve when they hear about Tyre.
verses.23:6: Cross over the seas; wail, you who dwell on the island!
verses.23:7: Is this not yours, she who boasted from earliest days in her antiquity? Her own feet will lead her far away to sojourn.
verses.23:8: Who has planned this against Tyre, once crowned, whose merchants were princes, her traders the renowned of the earth?
verses.23:9: The Lord of hosts has planned this, to pull down the pride of all glory and to bring to disgrace all the renowned of the earth.
verses.23:10: Pass through your land like a river, daughter of the sea! There is no longer a belt for you.
verses.23:11: He stretched out His hand over the sea; He threw kingdoms into turmoil. The Lord gave a command against Canaan to crush her strong ones,
verses.23:12: and He said: "You will no longer continue to boast, virgin daughter of Sidon, enduring oppression; rising up, cross over to Kittim; even there, there will be no rest for you."
verses.23:13: Look, the land of the Chaldeans: such a people did not exist; Assyria founded it; they led away its strong men into captivity, they undermined its houses, they turned it into a ruin.
verses.23:14: Wail, ships of the sea, for your stronghold has been devastated.
verses.23:15: And it will be on that day: you will be in oblivion, Tyre, for seventy years, like the days of one king; yet after seventy years, it will be for Tyre like the song of a prostitute:
verses.23:16: "Take up a harp, go around the city, prostitute given over to oblivion; sing well, repeat the song often, so that there may be remembrance of you."
verses.23:17: And it will be after seventy years: the Lord will visit Tyre, and He will bring her back to her wages, and she will again prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the earth upon the face of the earth;
verses.23:18: and her merchandise and her wages will be sanctified to the Lord; they will not be stored up nor laid away, for her merchandise will belong to those who dwell before the Lord, so that they may eat to fullness and be clothed until old age.
verses.24:1: Look, the Lord will devastate the earth, and will strip it bare, and will afflict its face, and will scatter its inhabitants.
verses.24:2: And it will be: as the people, so the priest; and as the servant, so his master; as the maidservant, so her mistress; as the buyer, so the one who sells; as the lender, so the one who takes a loan; as the one who demands repayment, so the one who owes.
verses.24:3: With devastation the earth will be devastated, and with plundering it will be despoiled; for the Lord has spoken this word.
verses.24:4: The earth has mourned and wasted away, and has grown weak; the world has wasted away, the loftiness of the people of the earth has grown weak.
verses.24:5: And the earth has been defiled by its inhabitants, because they have transgressed the laws, have altered the ordinance, have broken the everlasting covenant.
verses.24:6: Because of this a curse will devour the earth, and its inhabitants will sin; and therefore its cultivators will go mad, and few people will be left.
verses.24:7: The vintage has mourned, the vine has grown weak, all who were rejoicing in heart have groaned;
verses.24:8: the joy of tambourines has ceased, the sound of those rejoicing has grown quiet, the sweetness of the harp has fallen silent.
verses.24:9: With a song they will not drink wine; the drink will be bitter to those drinking it.
verses.24:10: The city of emptiness has been shattered, every house has been shut, with no one entering.
verses.24:11: There will be an outcry over wine in the streets; all gladness has been deserted, the joy of the earth has been carried away.
verses.24:12: Desolation has been left in the city, and calamity will crush the gates.
verses.24:13: For these things will be in the midst of the earth, in the midst of the peoples, just as if a few olives that have remained are shaken from an olive tree, and grape clusters when the vintage has been finished.
verses.24:14: These will lift up their voice and will praise; when the Lord has been glorified, they will shout aloud from the sea.
verses.24:15: Because of this, in teachings glorify the Lord; in the islands of the sea, the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.24:16: From the ends of the earth we have heard praises, the glory of the Righteous One. And I said, "My secret to me, my secret to me. Woe to me! The treacherous have acted treacherously, and with the treachery of transgressors they have acted treacherously."
verses.24:17: Terror, and pit, and snare are upon you, you who are an inhabitant of the earth.
verses.24:18: And it will be: the one who flees from the sound of terror will fall into the pit, and the one who extricates himself from the pit will be caught by the snare; because the floodgates from on high have been opened, and the foundations of the earth will be violently shaken.
verses.24:19: With shattering the earth will be shattered, with crushing the earth will be crushed, with shaking the earth will be shaken;
verses.24:20: with swaying the earth will be swayed like a drunkard, and it will be carried off like a tent of a single night; and its iniquity will weigh it down, and it will collapse, and it will not rise again.
verses.24:21: And it will be: on that day the Lord will make a visitation upon the host of heaven on high, and upon the kings of the earth who are upon the earth;
verses.24:22: and they will be gathered together in the gathering of a single bundle into a pit, and they will be shut up there in prison, and after many days they will be visited.
verses.24:23: And the moon will blush, and the sun will be put to shame, when the Lord of hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and is glorified in the sight of His elders.
verses.25:1: Lord, You are my God; I will exalt You, and I will give thanks to Your name: for You have done wondrous things, faithful plans of old. Amen.
verses.25:2: Because You have turned the city into a heap, the strong city into a ruin, the house of foreigners, so that it is not a city and will never be built.
verses.25:3: For this reason a strong people will praise You; the city of mighty nations will fear You:
verses.25:4: because You have become strength to the poor, strength to the needy in his distress, a hope from the whirlwind, a shade from the heat; for the breath of the mighty is like a whirlwind driving against a wall.
verses.25:5: Like heat in drought, You will humble the uproar of foreigners; and as with heat under a scorching cloud, You will make the offshoot of the strong wither.
verses.25:6: And the Lord of hosts will make for all peoples on this mountain a banquet of rich foods, a banquet of vintage, of rich foods full of marrow, of vintage cleared of dregs.
verses.25:7: And on this mountain He will cast down headlong the face of the bond bound over all peoples, and the web which He has woven over all nations.
verses.25:8: He will cast down death headlong forever; and the Lord God will take away the tear from every face, and He will take away the reproach of His people from the whole earth: for the Lord has spoken.
verses.25:9: And one will say on that day, "Look, this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He will save us; this is the Lord, we have waited patiently for Him: we will exult and be glad in His salvation."
verses.25:10: For the hand of the Lord will rest on this mountain; and Moab will be threshed beneath Him, just as straw is crushed in a wagon.
verses.25:11: And he will stretch out his hands beneath Him just as one swimming stretches out to swim; and He will humble his glory with the dashing of his hands.
verses.25:12: And the fortifications of your lofty walls will collapse, and will be humbled, and will be pulled down to the earth, all the way to the dust.
verses.26:1: On that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: "Zion is the city of our strength; a savior will be set in it as a wall and a bulwark.
verses.26:2: Open the gates, and let a righteous nation enter, keeping the truth.
verses.26:3: The old error has departed: You will keep peace; peace, because we have hoped in You.
verses.26:4: You have hoped in the Lord through eternal ages, in the Lord God, strong forever.
verses.26:5: For He will bow down those who dwell on high; He will humble the lofty city: He will humble it all the way to the earth, He will pull it down all the way to the dust.
verses.26:6: The foot will trample it, the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy."
verses.26:7: The path of the righteous is straight; straight is the footpath of the righteous for walking.
verses.26:8: And in the path of Your judgments, Lord, we have waited patiently for You: Your name and Your remembrance are in the desire of the soul.
verses.26:9: My soul has desired You in the night, and indeed with my spirit in my inmost heart I will keep watch for You from early morning. When You carry out Your judgments on the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness.
verses.26:10: Let us show mercy to the wicked, and he will not learn righteousness; in the land of the holy ones he has done unjust things, and he will not see the glory of the Lord.
verses.26:11: Lord, let Your hand be lifted up, and let them not see; let the envious peoples see and be put to shame, and let fire devour Your enemies.
verses.26:12: Lord, You will give peace to us: for You have worked all our works for us.
verses.26:13: Lord our God, lords besides You have possessed us; in You alone let us remember Your name.
verses.26:14: Let the dying not live, let the giants not rise again: therefore You have visited and crushed them, and You have destroyed all memory of them.
verses.26:15: You have shown indulgence to the nation, Lord, You have shown indulgence to the nation: have You been glorified? You have extended far all the borders of the earth.
verses.26:16: Lord, in anguish they have sought You; in the tribulation of murmuring Your instruction was for them.
verses.26:17: Just as she who conceives, when she draws near to childbirth, cries out in pain in her pangs, so have we become before Your face, Lord.
verses.26:18: We have conceived, and as it were been in labor, and have given birth to wind. We have not brought about deliverances on the earth; therefore the inhabitants of the earth have not fallen.
verses.26:19: Your dead will live, those of mine who were killed will rise again. Awake and give praise, you who dwell in the dust, for Your dew is a dew of light, and You will pull down the land of the giants into ruin.
verses.26:20: Go, My people, enter into your inner rooms; shut your doors upon yourself, hide yourself for a brief moment, until the indignation passes by.
verses.26:21: For look, the Lord will go out from His place to visit the iniquity of the inhabitant of the earth against him; and the earth will reveal its blood, and will no longer cover those who were killed upon it.
verses.27:1: In that day the Lord will visit upon Leviathan, the bar serpent, and upon Leviathan, the twisted serpent, with His hard, great, and strong sword, and He will kill the sea monster that is in the sea.
verses.27:2: In that day the vineyard of pure wine will sing to Him.
verses.27:3: "I am the Lord who keeps her; suddenly I will give her drink. So that no visitation may perhaps be made against her, night and day I keep her.
verses.27:4: Indignation is not in Me. Who will make Me a thorn and a bramble in battle? I will stride upon it; I will burn it altogether.
verses.27:5: Or will he rather take hold of My strength? He will make peace with Me; peace he will make with Me."
verses.27:6: Those who enter with a rush to Jacob: Israel will blossom and sprout, and they will fill the face of the world with seed.
verses.27:7: Has He struck him according to the blow of the one striking him? Or just as He killed those of his who were put to death, so was he killed?
verses.27:8: In measure against measure, when she has been cast out, You will judge her; He has meditated in His hard spirit through the day of heat.
verses.27:9: Therefore, upon this, iniquity will be forgiven to the house of Jacob; and this is all the fruit: that his sin be taken away, when he has made all the stones of the altar like shattered stones of ash; the groves and the shrines will not stand.
verses.27:10: For the fortified city will be desolate; the beautiful one will be abandoned and left like a desert; there the calf will graze, and there it will lie down, and it will consume its tops.
verses.27:11: In dryness her harvests will be crushed. Women are coming and teaching her; for it is not a wise people; therefore He who made it will not have mercy on it, and He who formed it will not spare it.
verses.27:12: And it will be: in that day the Lord will strike from the channel of the river to the torrent of Egypt; and you will be gathered one by one, sons of Israel.
verses.27:13: And it will be: in that day a blast will be sounded on a great trumpet; and those who had been lost will come from the land of the Assyrians, and those who had been cast out in the land of Egypt, and they will worship the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
