verses.49:18: Lift up your eyes all around and see: all these have gathered together; they have come to you. "As I live," says the Lord, "surely with all these you will be clothed as with an ornament, and you will put them around yourself like a bride;
verses.49:19: for your deserts, and your desolate places, and the land of your ruin will now be too narrow because of the inhabitants; and those who were swallowing you up will be driven far away."
verses.49:20: Still the children of your barrenness will say in your ears, "The place is too narrow for me; make room for me so that I may dwell."
verses.49:21: And you will say in your heart, "Who bore these for me? I was barren and not giving birth, exiled and captive; and who raised these? I was abandoned and alone; and where were these?"
verses.49:22: This is what the Lord God says: "Look, I will lift up My hand to the nations, and to the peoples I will raise up My standard; and they will bring your sons in their arms, and they will carry your daughters on their shoulders.
verses.49:23: And kings will be your foster fathers, and queens your nurses; with their faces lowered to the ground they will bow down before you, and they will lick the dust of your feet. And you will know that I am the Lord, on account of whom those who wait for Him will not be put to shame."
verses.49:24: Can prey be taken from the mighty? Or can what has been captured by the strong be saved?
verses.49:25: For this is what the Lord says: "Indeed, even the captives will be taken from the mighty, and what has been carried off by the strong will be saved. And those who have judged you I will judge, and your children I will save.
verses.49:26: And I will feed your enemies with their own flesh, and as with new wine, they will become drunk with their own blood; and all flesh will know that I am the Lord who saves you, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob."
verses.50:1: This is what the Lord says: "What is this bill of divorce of your mother, by which I sent her away? Or who is My creditor, to whom I sold you? Look, for your iniquities you were sold, and for your crimes I sent your mother away.
verses.50:2: For I came, and there was no man; I called, and there was no one to hear. Has My hand been shortened and made small, so that I cannot redeem? Or is there no power in Me to deliver? Look, at My rebuke I will make the sea a desert, I will turn the rivers into dry ground; the fish will rot without water and die of thirst.
verses.50:3: I will clothe the heavens with darkness, and I will make sackcloth their covering."
verses.50:4: The Lord has given me a learned tongue, so that I may know how to sustain with a word the one who is weary. He rouses in the morning, in the morning He rouses my ear, so that I may listen as to a master.
verses.50:5: The Lord God has opened my ear, and I do not contradict Him; I have not turned back.
verses.50:6: I gave my body to those who struck me, and my cheeks to those who plucked them; I did not turn my face away from those who reproached me and spat on me.
verses.50:7: The Lord God is my helper, therefore I have not been put to shame; therefore I have set my face like a very hard rock, and I know that I will not be put to shame.
verses.50:8: He who justifies me is near; who will contradict me? Let us stand together; who is my adversary? Let him come near to me.
verses.50:9: Look, the Lord God is my helper; who is there who will condemn me? Look, all of them will be worn out like a garment; the moth will eat them.
verses.50:10: Who among you fears the Lord, hearing the voice of His servant? He who has walked in darkness and has no light, let him hope in the name of the Lord and lean upon his God.
verses.50:11: Look, all you who kindle a fire, armed with flames: walk in the light of your fire and in the flames that you have set ablaze; from My hand this has happened to you: in sorrows you will sleep.
verses.51:1: Listen to Me, you who pursue what is righteous and seek the Lord; look to the rock from which you were cut out, and to the hollow of the pit from which you were carved out.
verses.51:2: Look to Abraham, your father, and to Sarah, who gave birth to you; for I called him when he was one, and I blessed him and multiplied him.
verses.51:3: Therefore the Lord will comfort Zion, and He will comfort all her ruins; He will make her desert like delights, and her wilderness like the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the voice of praise.
verses.51:4: Pay attention to Me, My people, and My tribe, listen to Me; for a law will go out from Me, and My judgment will rest as a light for the peoples.
verses.51:5: My righteous one is near, My savior has gone out, and My arms will judge the peoples; the islands will wait for Me, and they will wait upon My arm.
verses.51:6: Lift up your eyes to heaven, and look beneath the earth below; for the heavens will dissolve like smoke, and the earth will be worn away like a garment, and its inhabitants will perish like these; but My salvation will be forever, and My righteousness will not fail.
verses.51:7: Listen to Me, you who know what is righteous, My people, with My law in their heart: do not fear the reproach of men, and do not dread their blasphemies;
verses.51:8: for the worm will eat them just like a garment, and the moth will devour them just like wool; but My salvation will be forever, and My righteousness for generations of generations.
verses.51:9: Rise up, rise up, put on strength, arm of the Lord! Rise up as in ancient days, in the generations of the ages. Was it not You who struck the proud one, who wounded the dragon?
verses.51:10: Was it not You who dried up the sea, the water of the mighty abyss, who made the depth of the sea a way so that those set free might cross over?
verses.51:11: And now those who have been redeemed by the Lord will return and come into Zion praising, with everlasting gladness upon their heads; they will hold joy and gladness, and sorrow and groaning will flee.
verses.51:12: I, I Myself will comfort you. Who are you, that you should be afraid of a mortal man, and of a son of man who will dry up just like grass?
verses.51:13: And you have forgotten the Lord, your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundation of the earth; and you have been terrified continually all day long before the face of the fury of the one who oppressed you and had prepared to destroy. Where now is the fury of the oppressor?
verses.51:14: Quickly the one advancing to open will come; and he will not kill to utter destruction, nor will his bread fail.
verses.51:15: But I am the Lord your God, who stir up the sea, and its waves swell; the Lord of hosts is My name.
verses.51:16: I have placed My words in your mouth, and in the shadow of My hand I have protected you, so that you may plant the heavens and lay the foundation of the earth, and say to Zion, "You are My people."
verses.51:17: Lift yourself up, lift yourself up, rise up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the Lord the cup of His wrath; down to the bottom of the cup of stupor you have drunk, and you have drunk deeply down to the dregs.
verses.51:18: There is no one to uphold her out of all the sons whom she bore, and there is no one to take hold of her hand out of all the sons whom she nurtured.
verses.51:19: There are two things that have come upon you; who will grieve over you? Devastation and shattering, and famine and the sword; who will comfort you?
verses.51:20: Your sons have been cast down; they have slept at the head of all the streets like an ensnared oryx, full of the indignation of the Lord, of the rebuke of your God.
verses.51:21: Therefore listen to this, poor little one, and drunk, not from wine.
verses.51:22: Your Ruler, the Lord, and your God, who will fight for His people, says this: "Look, I have taken from your hand the cup of stupor, the bottom of the cup of My indignation; you will not drink it anymore.
verses.51:23: And I will place it in the hand of those who humiliated you and said to your soul, 'Bow down, so that we may pass over'; and you laid your body like the ground, and like a way for those passing over."
verses.52:1: Rise up, rise up, put on your strength, Zion! Put on the garments of your glory, Jerusalem, city of the Holy One, for the uncircumcised and the unclean will no longer pass through you.
verses.52:2: Shake yourself from the dust, rise up; sit down, Jerusalem! Loosen the bonds of your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
verses.52:3: For the Lord says this: "You were sold for nothing, and without silver you will be redeemed."
verses.52:4: For the Lord God says this: "My people went down into Egypt at the beginning to be a settler there, and Assyria oppressed them without any cause.
verses.52:5: And now what do I have here," says the Lord, "since My people have been taken away for nothing? Their rulers act unjustly," says the Lord, "and continually all day long My name is blasphemed.
verses.52:6: Because of this, My people will know My name on that day, for I Myself who was speaking, look, here I am."
verses.52:7: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the one announcing and proclaiming peace, announcing good, proclaiming salvation, saying to Zion, "Your God will reign!"
verses.52:8: The voice of your watchmen: they have lifted up their voice, together they will praise, for eye to eye they will see when the Lord brings Zion back.
verses.52:9: Rejoice and praise together, desolate places of Jerusalem, for the Lord has comforted His people; He has redeemed Jerusalem.
verses.52:10: The Lord has prepared His holy arm in the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
verses.52:11: Depart, depart; go out from there, do not touch what is polluted; go out from the midst of it; be cleansed, you who carry the vessels of the Lord.
verses.52:12: For you will not go out in tumult, nor will you hurry in flight; for the Lord will go before you, and the God of Israel will gather you.
verses.52:13: Look, My servant will understand; He will be exalted and lifted up, and He will be exceedingly high.
verses.52:14: Just as many were astounded at You, so inglorious will His appearance be among men, and His form among the sons of men.
verses.52:15: He will sprinkle many nations; before Him kings will hold their mouths shut, for those to whom it has not been told about Him have seen, and those who have not heard have contemplated.
verses.53:1: Who has believed our report? And the arm of the Lord, to whom has it been revealed?
verses.53:2: And he will grow up like a young shoot before Him, and like a root out of thirsty ground. There is no beauty in him nor splendor; and we saw him, and there was no appearance, and we desired him:
verses.53:3: despised and the lowest of men, a man of sorrows and acquainted with weakness; and his face was as if hidden and despised, on account of which we did not esteem him.
verses.53:4: Truly he himself bore our weaknesses, and he himself carried our sorrows; yet we considered him like a leper, and struck by God and humbled.
verses.53:5: Yet he himself was wounded on account of our iniquities; he was crushed on account of our crimes. The discipline of our peace was upon him, and by his bruise we have been healed.
verses.53:6: All of us like sheep have gone astray, each one has turned aside to his own way; and the Lord has laid upon him the iniquity of us all.
verses.53:7: He was offered up because he himself willed it, and he did not open his mouth; like a sheep he will be led to slaughter, and like a lamb before the one shearing it he will fall silent, and he will not open his mouth.
verses.53:8: From distress and from judgment he was taken away. Who will recount his generation? For he was cut off from the land of the living; on account of the crime of My people I struck him.
verses.53:9: And he will give the wicked for his burial, and the rich man for his death, because he had committed no iniquity, nor was there deceit in his mouth.
verses.53:10: And the Lord willed to crush him in weakness. If he lays down his soul for sin, he will see long-lived offspring, and the will of the Lord will be directed in his hand.
verses.53:11: Because of what his soul has labored through, he will see and be satisfied. By his knowledge My righteous servant himself will justify many, and he himself will carry their iniquities.
verses.53:12: Therefore I will allot to him very many, and he will divide the spoils of the strong, because he handed over his soul to death and was counted with criminals, and he himself bore the sins of many and pleaded for transgressors.
verses.54:1: "Praise, barren woman, you who do not give birth; sing out praise and cry out joyfully, you who were not giving birth, for the children of the desolate woman are many, more than those of her who has a husband," says the Lord.
verses.54:2: "Enlarge the place of your tent, and stretch out the skins of your dwellings; do not hold back; make your cords long, and make your stakes firm.
verses.54:3: For to the right and to the left you will press forward, and your offspring will inherit the nations and will inhabit the desolate cities.
verses.54:4: Do not fear, for you will not be put to shame, nor will you blush; for you will not feel disgrace, because you will forget the shame of your youth, and the reproach of your widowhood you will remember no longer.
verses.54:5: For He who made you will rule over you, the Lord of hosts is His name, and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; He will be called the God of all the earth.
verses.54:6: For the Lord has called you like a woman abandoned and grieving in spirit, and like a wife cast off from youth," your God has said.
verses.54:7: "For a brief instant I abandoned you, and with great compassions I will gather you.
verses.54:8: In a moment of indignation I hid My face from you for a little while, and with everlasting mercy I have had compassion on you," your Redeemer, the Lord, has said.
verses.54:9: "This is to Me just as in the days of Noah, to whom I swore that I would not bring the waters of Noah upon the earth anymore; so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you and will not rebuke you.
verses.54:10: For the mountains will be moved, and the hills will tremble; yet My mercy will not depart from you, and the covenant of My peace will not be moved," the Lord, who has compassion on you, has said.
verses.54:11: "Poor little one, torn by the storm without any comfort, look, I will lay your stones in order, and I will lay your foundations in sapphires;
verses.54:12: and I will make your battlements of jasper, and your gates of carved stones, and all your borders of desirable stones,
verses.54:13: all your children taught by the Lord, and an abundance of peace for your children.
verses.54:14: And in righteousness you will be founded; depart far from oppression, for you will not fear, and from terror, for it will not draw near to you.
verses.54:15: Look, a resident alien will come who was not with Me; one who was once a stranger to you will be joined to you.
verses.54:16: Look, I have created the smith who blows on the coals in the fire and brings forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the killer to destroy.
verses.54:17: No instrument that has been fashioned against you will succeed, and every tongue resisting you in judgment you will judge. This is the inheritance of the servants of the Lord, and their righteousness is with Me," says the Lord.
verses.55:1: All you who are thirsty, come to the waters, and you who have no silver, hurry, buy, and eat; come, buy wine and milk without silver and without any exchange.
verses.55:2: Why do you weigh out silver for what is not bread, and your labor for what brings no satisfaction? Listen closely to Me, and eat what is good, and your soul will delight in richness.
verses.55:3: Incline your ear, and come to Me; listen, and your soul will live, and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, the faithful mercies of David.
verses.55:4: Look, I have given him as a witness to the peoples, a leader and instructor to the nations.
verses.55:5: Look, you will call a nation that you did not know, and nations that have not known you will run to you, because of the Lord your God, and the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you.
verses.55:6: Seek the Lord while He can be found; call upon Him while He is near.
verses.55:7: Let the wicked one abandon his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts, and let him return to the Lord, and He will have mercy on him; and to our God, for He is abundant in forgiving.
verses.55:8: "For My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways My ways," says the Lord.
verses.55:9: "For just as the heavens are exalted above the earth, so are My ways exalted above your ways, and My thoughts above your thoughts.
verses.55:10: And just as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there again, but saturate the earth, and water it, and make it sprout, and give seed to the one who sows, and bread to the one who eats,
verses.55:11: so will My word be that goes out from My mouth; it will not return to Me empty, but it will do whatever I have willed, and it will prosper in the things for which I sent it."
verses.55:12: For you will go out in joy, and be led on in peace; the mountains and the hills will sing praise before you, and all the trees of the region will clap their hands.
verses.55:13: Instead of the brier the fir tree will come up, and instead of the nettle the myrtle will grow; and the Lord will be renowned as an eternal sign that will not be taken away.
verses.56:1: This is what the Lord says: "Keep justice, and practice righteousness, for My salvation is near to come, and My righteousness to be revealed."
verses.56:2: Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who will take hold of it, keeping the Sabbath so that he does not defile it, keeping his hands so that he does not do any evil.
verses.56:3: And let not the son of the foreigner who clings to the Lord speak, saying, "The Lord will surely divide me from His people," and let not the eunuch say, "Look, I am a dry tree."
verses.56:4: For this is what the Lord says to the eunuchs: "Those who keep My Sabbaths, and choose the things that I have willed, and hold fast to My covenant,
verses.56:5: to them I will give in My house and within My walls a place, and a name better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name that will not perish.
verses.56:6: And the sons of the foreigner who cling to the Lord, to worship Him, and to love His name, to be servants to Him, everyone who keeps the Sabbath so that he does not defile it, and who holds fast to My covenant,
verses.56:7: I will bring them to My holy mountain, and I will make them joyful in My house of prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be pleasing to Me on My altar, for My house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples."
verses.56:8: The Lord God, who gathers the dispersed of Israel, says: "I will still gather to him his gathered ones."
verses.56:9: All you beasts of the field, come to devour, all the beasts of the forest.
verses.56:10: Its watchmen are all blind; all of them know nothing: mute dogs unable to bark, seeing empty things, sleeping, and loving dreams.
verses.56:11: And the most imprudent dogs have not known satisfaction; the shepherds themselves have been ignorant of understanding: all of them have turned aside to their own way, each one to his own greed, from the highest to the last.
verses.57:1: The righteous one perishes, and there is no one who reflects in his heart; and men of mercy are gathered away, because there is no one who understands: for the righteous one has been gathered away from the face of evil.
verses.57:2: Let peace come; let him rest in his bed who has walked in his uprightness.
verses.57:3: But you, draw near here, sons of a female diviner, offspring of an adulterer and a prostitute.
verses.57:4: At whom have you mocked? At whom have you opened wide your mouth and thrust out your tongue? Are you not wicked sons, lying offspring,
verses.57:5: who console yourselves in gods under every leafy tree, sacrificing little children in the streambeds, beneath the overhanging rocks?
verses.57:6: Among the portions of the streambed is your portion; this is your lot: to them also you poured out a drink offering, you offered a sacrifice. Will I not be indignant over these things?
verses.57:7: On a high and lofty mountain you placed your bed, and there you went up to offer sacrifices.
verses.57:8: And behind the door and behind the doorpost you placed your memorial. Because beside Me you uncovered yourself, and received an adulterer, you widened your bed, and made a covenant with them; you loved their couch with an open hand.
verses.57:9: And you adorned yourself for the king with ointment, and multiplied your perfumes. You sent your envoys far away, and you were humbled all the way down to the underworld.
verses.57:10: In the great extent of your way you grew weary; you did not say, "I will rest." You found the life of your hand; therefore you did not plead.
verses.57:11: For whom were you anxious and afraid, that you lied, and did not remember Me, nor think of it in your heart? Because I am silent and as though not seeing, you have forgotten Me.
verses.57:12: I will declare your righteousness, and your works will not benefit you.
verses.57:13: When you cry out, let your gathered ones rescue you; and the wind will carry them all away, a breeze will lift them off. But the one who has trust in Me will inherit the land, and will possess My holy mountain.
verses.57:14: And I will say, "Make a way, prepare a road; turn aside from the path, remove the stumbling blocks from the way of My people."
verses.57:15: For this is what the High and Exalted One says, who inhabits eternity, and His name is holy, dwelling in the high and holy place and with a contrite and humble spirit, so that He may revive the spirit of the humble and revive the heart of the contrite:
verses.57:16: "For I will not contend forever, nor will I be angry to the end, because a spirit will go out from My presence, and I Myself will make breaths.
verses.57:17: Because of the iniquity of his greed I was angry, and I struck him. I hid My face from you, and I was indignant; and he went away wandering in the way of his heart.
verses.57:18: I have seen his ways, and I have healed him; and I have led him back, and I have restored consolations to him and to his mourners.
verses.57:19: I have created the fruit of the lips, peace; peace to the one who is far off and to the one who is near," said the Lord, "and I have healed him."
verses.57:20: But the wicked are like a churning sea, which cannot rest, and its waves overflow into trampling and mud.
verses.57:21: "There is no peace for the wicked," says the Lord God.
verses.58:1: Cry out, do not cease; like a trumpet, raise your voice high, and announce to My people their crimes, and to the house of Jacob their sins.
verses.58:2: For indeed they seek Me from day to day, and they desire to know My ways, like a nation that has practiced righteousness and has not abandoned the judgment of its God. They ask Me for judgments of righteousness; they desire to draw near to God.
verses.58:3: "Why have we fasted, and You did not look? We have humbled our souls, and You did not know?" Look, on the day of your fast your will is found, and you demand payment from all your debtors.
verses.58:4: Look, you fast for disputes and contentions, and you strike wickedly with the fist. Do not fast as you have up to this day, so that your outcry may be heard on high.
verses.58:5: Is such the fast that I have chosen, for a man to afflict his soul for a day? Is it to twist his head like a circle, and to spread out sackcloth and ashes? Will you call this a fast, and a day acceptable to the Lord?
verses.58:6: Is not this rather the fast that I have chosen? Loosen the bonds of wickedness, untie the oppressive bundles, let those who are crushed go free, and break apart every burden;
verses.58:7: break your bread for the hungry, and bring the needy and wandering into your house; when you see someone naked, cover him, and do not despise your flesh.
verses.58:8: Then your light will break forth like the morning, and your healing will swiftly rise; and your righteousness will go before your face, and the glory of the Lord will gather you.
verses.58:9: Then you will call, and the Lord will hear; you will cry out, and He will say, "Here I am." If you remove the chain from your midst, and cease stretching out the finger and speaking what does not profit,
verses.58:10: when you pour out your soul to the hungry and fill the afflicted soul, your light will rise in the darkness, and your darkness will be like noon.
verses.58:11: And the Lord will give you rest always, and He will fill your soul with splendors, and He will deliver your bones; and you will be like a watered garden, and like a spring of waters whose waters will not fail.
verses.58:12: And the desolate places of the ages will be built in you; you will raise up the foundations of generation and generation; and you will be called a builder of hedges, turning paths into quietness.
verses.58:13: If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your will on My holy day, and call the Sabbath delightful, and the holy day of the Lord glorious, and glorify Him while you do not follow your ways, and your will is not found so as to speak a word,
verses.58:14: then you will take delight in the Lord, and I will lift you up above the heights of the earth, and I will feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.
verses.59:1: Look, the hand of the Lord is not shortened so that it cannot save, nor is His ear weighed down so that it cannot hear.
verses.59:2: But your iniquities have divided between you and your God, and your sins have hidden His face from you, so that He would not hear.
verses.59:3: For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken falsehood, and your tongue utters iniquity.
verses.59:4: There is no one who calls upon righteousness, nor is there anyone who judges truthfully; instead they trust in nothing and speak empty things; they have conceived trouble and given birth to iniquity.
verses.59:5: They have broken open the eggs of asps and woven spider webs. Whoever eats from their eggs will die, and what is warmed will burst forth into a basilisk.
verses.59:6: Their webs will not become clothing, nor will they cover themselves with their works; their works are useless works, and a work of iniquity is in their hands.
verses.59:7: Their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood; their thoughts are useless thoughts; devastation and destruction are in their ways.
verses.59:8: They have not known the way of peace, and there is no justice in their steps; their paths have been made crooked for them; everyone who treads on them is ignorant of peace.
verses.59:9: Because of this, justice is far removed from us, and righteousness will not overtake us. We waited for light, and look, darkness; for brightness, and we walked in darkness.
verses.59:10: We groped for the wall like the blind, and as if without eyes we felt our way; we stumbled at noon as if in darkness, in gloomy places like the dead.
verses.59:11: We will all roar like bears, and like meditating doves we will moan; we waited for justice, and there is none; for salvation, and it is far removed from us.
verses.59:12: For our iniquities have been multiplied before You, and our sins have answered us, because our crimes are with us, and we know our iniquities.
verses.59:13: Sinning and lying against the Lord, and we have turned away so that we would not go after our God, so as to speak slander and transgression; we have conceived and spoken from the heart words of falsehood.
verses.59:14: And justice has been turned backward, and righteousness has stood far off, because truth has fallen in the public square, and equity could not enter.
verses.59:15: And truth has passed into oblivion, and the one who turned away from evil lay open to plunder. And the Lord saw, and it appeared evil in His eyes, because there is no justice.
verses.59:16: And He saw that there is no man, and He was perplexed because there is no one who steps forward; and His own arm brought salvation for Him, and His righteousness itself upheld Him.
verses.59:17: He clothed Himself with righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on His head; He clothed Himself with garments of vengeance, and covered Himself as with a cloak of zeal,
verses.59:18: as for vengeance, as for repayment of indignation to His adversaries, and requital to His enemies; to the islands He will pay back in kind.
verses.59:19: And those from the west will fear the name of the Lord, and those from the rising of the sun His glory, when He comes like a violent river which the Spirit of the Lord drives on,
verses.59:20: and a Redeemer comes to Zion, and to those who return from iniquity in Jacob, says the Lord.
verses.59:21: "This is My covenant with them," says the Lord: "My Spirit who is in you, and My words which I have put in your mouth, will not depart from your mouth, and from the mouth of your offspring, and from the mouth of the offspring of your offspring," says the Lord, "from now on and forevermore."
verses.60:1: Rise up, be illumined, Jerusalem, because your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.
verses.60:2: For look, darkness will cover the earth, and gloom the peoples; but upon you the Lord will rise, and His glory will be seen in you.
verses.60:3: And nations will walk in your light, and kings in the brightness of your rising.
verses.60:4: Lift up your eyes all around and see: all these have been gathered together, they have come to you; your sons will come from afar, and your daughters will rise from the side.
verses.60:5: Then you will see and overflow; your heart will marvel and be enlarged, when the multitude of the sea is turned to you, when the strength of the nations comes to you.
verses.60:6: A flood of camels will cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all from Sheba will come, bringing gold and frankincense, and announcing praise to the Lord.
verses.60:7: All the flock of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth will minister to you; they will be offered upon My acceptable altar, and I will glorify the house of My majesty.
verses.60:8: Who are these who fly like clouds, and like doves to their windows?
verses.60:9: For the islands wait for Me, and the ships of the sea at the first, so that I may bring your sons from afar, their silver and their gold with them, for the name of the Lord your God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because He has glorified you.
verses.60:10: And the sons of foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will minister to you; for in My indignation I struck you, and in My reconciliation I have had mercy on you.
verses.60:11: And your gates will be opened continually; day and night they will not be shut, so that the strength of the nations may be brought to you, and their kings may be led in.
verses.60:12: For the nation and the kingdom that will not serve you will perish, and the nations will be laid waste with desolation.
verses.60:13: The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the fir, and the box tree, and the pine together, to adorn the place of My sanctuary; and I will glorify the place of My feet.
verses.60:14: And the sons of those who humbled you will come to you bowed down, and all who spoke against you will bow down to the footprints of your feet; and they will call you the City of the Lord, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.60:15: Because you have been abandoned and hated, and there was no one who passed through you, I will make you the pride of the ages, a joy for generation and generation;
verses.60:16: and you will nurse from the milk of the nations, and be suckled at the breast of kings; and you will know that I am the Lord who saves you, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
verses.60:17: Instead of bronze I will bring gold, and instead of iron I will bring silver, and instead of wood, bronze, and instead of stones, iron; and I will make your visitation peace, and your overseers righteousness.
verses.60:18: Iniquity will no longer be heard in your land, nor devastation and destruction within your borders; and salvation will occupy your walls, and praise your gates.
verses.60:19: You will no longer have the sun to shine by day, nor will the brightness of the moon illumine you; but the Lord will be an everlasting light for you, and your God your glory.
verses.60:20: Your sun will no longer set, and your moon will not be diminished, because the Lord will be an everlasting light for you, and the days of your mourning will be completed.
verses.60:21: And your people will all be righteous; they will inherit the land forever, the shoot of My planting, the work of My hand, for glorifying.
verses.60:22: The least will become a thousand, and the little one a most mighty nation. I, the Lord, will suddenly do this in its time.
verses.61:1: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; He sent me to preach to the meek, to heal those crushed in heart, and to proclaim pardon to the captives and opening to those confined;
verses.61:2: to proclaim a year favorable to the Lord and a day of vengeance for our God; to comfort all who mourn,
verses.61:3: to provide for the mourners of Zion and give them a crown instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, a cloak of praise instead of a spirit of grief; and they will be called in her mighty ones of righteousness, the planting of the Lord for glorification.
verses.61:4: And they will build the places deserted from ages past, and they will raise up the ancient ruins, and they will restore the deserted cities, laid waste for generation after generation.
verses.61:5: And strangers will stand and pasture your flocks, and the sons of foreigners will be your farmers and your vinedressers.
verses.61:6: But you will be called priests of the Lord; "Ministers of our God," it will be said to you; you will eat the strength of the nations, and in their glory you will take pride.
verses.61:7: Instead of your double shame and disgrace, they will praise their portion; because of this, in their land they will possess a double share; everlasting gladness will be theirs.
verses.61:8: For I, the Lord, love justice and hate robbery in a burnt offering; and I will give their work in truth, and I will make a perpetual covenant with them.
verses.61:9: And they will know their seed among the nations, and their offspring in the midst of the peoples; all who see them will recognize them, that these are the seed whom the Lord has blessed.
verses.61:10: Rejoicing, I will rejoice in the Lord, and my soul will exult in my God, because He has clothed me with garments of salvation and has wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, like a bridegroom adorned with a crown, and like a bride ornamented with her jewels.
verses.61:11: For just as the earth brings forth its sprout, and just as a garden makes its seed sprout, so the Lord God will make righteousness and praise sprout before all the nations.
verses.62:1: For the sake of Zion I will not keep silent, and for the sake of Jerusalem I will not rest, until her righteous one goes forth like brightness, and her savior is kindled like a torch.
verses.62:2: And the nations will see your righteous one, and all the kings your renowned one; and a new name will be called for you, which the mouth of the Lord will name.
verses.62:3: And you will be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a diadem of the kingdom in the hand of your God.
verses.62:4: You will no longer be called "Abandoned," and your land will no more be called "Desolate"; but you will be called "My Will Is in Her," and your land "Inhabited," because the Lord has been well pleased in you, and your land will be inhabited.
verses.62:5: For a young man will dwell with a virgin, and your sons will dwell in you; and a bridegroom will rejoice over a bride, and your God will rejoice over you.
verses.62:6: Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen; all day and all night perpetually they will not keep silent. You who remember the Lord, do not keep silent,
verses.62:7: and give Him no silence, until He establishes and until He makes Jerusalem a praise on the earth.
verses.62:8: The Lord has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength: "Never again will I give your wheat as food to your enemies, and foreign sons will not drink your wine for which you have labored;
verses.62:9: for those who gather it will eat and praise the Lord, and those who carry it in will drink in My holy courts."
verses.62:10: Pass through, pass through the gates, prepare the way for the people; make the road level, pick out the stones, and lift up a standard to the peoples.
verses.62:11: Look, the Lord has made it heard at the ends of the earth: "Say to the daughter of Zion, 'Look, your Savior comes; look, His reward is with Him, and His work is before Him.'"
verses.62:12: And they will call them "Holy People, Redeemed by the Lord"; but you will be called "Sought-Out City," and not "Abandoned."
verses.63:1: "Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? This splendid One in His long robe, striding in the abundance of His strength?" "It is I, who speak righteousness, and am a defender to save."
verses.63:2: "Why then is Your robe red, and Your garments like those of treaders in a winepress?"
verses.63:3: "I have trodden the winepress alone, and from the nations there is no man with Me; I trod them in My fury and trampled them in My wrath; and their blood was spattered upon My garments, and I have stained all My robes.
verses.63:4: For the day of vengeance is in My heart; the year of My redemption has come.
verses.63:5: I looked around, and there was no helper; I sought, and there was no one to assist; and My arm brought salvation to Me, and My indignation itself helped Me.
verses.63:6: And I trampled the peoples in My fury, and made them drunk in My indignation, and dragged down their strength to the earth."
verses.63:7: I will remember the compassions of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all that the Lord has rendered to us, and for the abundance of good things to the house of Israel, which He has generously bestowed upon them according to His forbearance and according to the abundance of His mercies.
verses.63:8: And He said, "Surely they are My people, sons who do not deny"; and He became a savior to them.
verses.63:9: In all their affliction He was not afflicted, and the angel of His face saved them; in His love and in His forbearance He Himself redeemed them, and carried them, and lifted them up all the days of old.
verses.63:10: But they themselves provoked Him to anger and afflicted the Spirit of His Holy One; and He turned into an enemy against them, and He Himself waged war against them.
verses.63:11: And He remembered the days of old, of Moses and of His people. Where is He who led them out of the sea with the shepherds of His flock? Where is He who placed in its midst the Spirit of His Holy One,
verses.63:12: who led Moses out at the right hand by the arm of His majesty; who split the waters before them to make for Himself an everlasting name;
verses.63:13: who led them out through the depths, like a horse in the desert that does not stumble?
verses.63:14: Like an animal going down into a plain, the Spirit of the Lord was its leader. Thus You led Your people to make for Yourself a name of glory.
verses.63:15: Look down from heaven, and see from Your holy dwelling place, and that of Your glory. Where is Your zeal and Your strength, the abundance of Your tender affections and of Your compassions? Toward me they have held themselves back.
verses.63:16: For You are our Father, and Abraham did not know us, and Israel did not recognize us; You, Lord, are our Father, our Redeemer; Your name is from ages past.
verses.63:17: Why have You made us wander, Lord, from Your ways, and hardened our heart so that we would not fear You? Return for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your inheritance.
verses.63:18: As nothing they have possessed Your holy people; our foes have trampled Your sanctuary.
verses.63:19: We have become as in the beginning, when You did not rule over us, nor was Your name invoked over us.
verses.64:1: As by the burning of fire they would melt, waters would burn with fire, so that Your name would be made known to Your enemies; before Your face the nations would be thrown into turmoil.
verses.64:2: When You do wonders, we will not endure; You came down, and before Your face the mountains flowed down.
verses.64:3: From ages past they have not heard, nor perceived with their ears; no eye has seen, God, apart from You, the things You have prepared for those who wait for You.
verses.64:4: You have met the one who is glad and does righteousness; in Your ways they will remember You. Look, You were angry, and we have sinned; in them we have always been, and we will be saved.
verses.64:5: And all of us have become like someone unclean, and all our righteous deeds are like the cloth of a menstruating woman; and all of us have fallen like a leaf, and our iniquities, like the wind, have carried us away.
verses.64:6: There is no one who calls on Your name, who rises up and takes hold of You. You have hidden Your face from us, and You have crushed us in the hand of our iniquity.
verses.64:7: And now, Lord, You are our Father, while we are clay; You are our potter, and all of us are the works of Your hands.
verses.64:8: Do not be exceedingly angry, Lord, and do not remember our iniquity any longer; now look: all of us are Your people.
verses.64:9: The city of Your Holy One has become deserted; Zion has become deserted; Jerusalem is desolate.
verses.64:10: The house of our sanctification and our glory, where our fathers praised You, has become a burning of fire, and all our desirable things have been turned into ruins.
verses.64:11: Will You restrain Yourself over these things, Lord? Will You keep silent and afflict us severely?
verses.65:1: Those who did not ask before have sought Me; those who did not seek Me have found Me. I said, "Here I am, here I am," to a nation that did not call on My name.
verses.65:2: I have stretched out My hands all day long to an unbelieving people who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts;
verses.65:3: a people who provoke Me to anger before My face continually, who offer sacrifices in gardens and make offerings on bricks;
verses.65:4: who dwell in tombs and sleep in the shrines of idols; who eat pig's flesh, and profane broth is in their vessels;
verses.65:5: who say, "Withdraw from me; do not come near me, because you are unclean." These will be smoke in My fury, a fire burning all day long.
verses.65:6: Look, it is written before Me: "I will not keep silent, but I will repay, and I will pay back into their bosom,
verses.65:7: your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together," says the Lord, "who sacrificed on the mountains and reproached Me on the hills; and I will measure back their former work into their bosom."
verses.65:8: This is what the Lord says: "Just as when a grape is found in a cluster, and it is said, 'Do not destroy it, for it is a blessing,' so I will do for the sake of My servants, so that I will not destroy the whole.
verses.65:9: And I will bring forth offspring from Jacob, and from Judah one who possesses My mountains; and My chosen ones will inherit it, and My servants will dwell there.
verses.65:10: And the plains will become folds for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for herds, for My people who have sought Me.
verses.65:11: And you who have abandoned the Lord, who have forgotten My holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and pour drink offerings on it:
verses.65:12: I will number you for the sword, and all of you will collapse in slaughter, because I called and you did not answer; I spoke and you did not hear; and you did evil in My eyes, and you chose the things I did not want."
verses.65:13: Therefore, this is what the Lord God says: "Look, My servants will eat, and you will be hungry; look, My servants will drink, and you will be thirsty;
verses.65:14: look, My servants will be glad, and you will be put to shame; look, My servants will give praise out of exultation of heart, and you will cry out from sorrow of heart, and from brokenness of spirit you will wail,
verses.65:15: and you will leave your name as an oath for My chosen ones; and the Lord God will put you to death, and He will call His servants by another name:
verses.65:16: by which the one who is blessed on the earth will be blessed in God, amen, and the one who swears in the earth will swear by God, amen: because the former distresses have been handed over to forgetfulness, and because they are hidden from My eyes.
verses.65:17: For look, I am creating new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be in memory, and they will not rise up upon the heart.
verses.65:18: Rather, you will rejoice and exult forever in the things that I create; for look, I am creating Jerusalem to be an exultation, and her people a joy.
verses.65:19: And I will exult in Jerusalem, and I will rejoice in My people; and there will no longer be heard in it the voice of weeping and the voice of outcry.
verses.65:20: There will no longer be there an infant of days, nor an old man who does not complete his days, for the child of a hundred years will die, and the sinner of a hundred years will be cursed.
verses.65:21: And they will build houses and dwell in them; and they will plant vineyards and eat their fruits.
verses.65:22: They will not build and another dwell there; they will not plant and another eat: for according to the days of a tree will be the days of My people, and the works of their hands will grow old.
verses.65:23: My chosen ones will not labor in vain, nor bring forth children in turmoil, for they are the offspring of the blessed of the Lord, and their descendants are with them.
verses.65:24: And it will happen that before they cry out, I will answer; while they are still speaking, I will hear.
verses.65:25: The wolf and the lamb will graze together, the lion and the ox will eat straw, and for the serpent, dust will be its bread. They will not harm nor kill in all My holy mountain," says the Lord.
verses.66:1: This is what the Lord says: "Heaven is My throne, and the earth is the footstool of My feet. What is this house that you will build for Me? And what is this place of My rest?
verses.66:2: All these things My hand has made, and all these came into being," says the Lord. "Yet to whom will I look, except to the poor one, and the one contrite in spirit, and the one who trembles at My words?
verses.66:3: The one who sacrifices an ox is like one who kills a man; the one who slaughters a beast is like one who dashes out the brains of a dog; the one who offers an offering is like one who offers pig's blood; the one who remembers frankincense is like one who blesses an idol. All these things they have chosen in their ways, and their soul has delighted in their abominations.
verses.66:4: Therefore I also will choose their delusions, and I will bring upon them the things they feared; because I called, and there was no one who answered; I spoke, and they did not hear; and they did evil in My eyes, and they chose the things I did not want."
verses.66:5: Hear the word of the Lord, you who tremble at His word. Your brothers who hate you and cast you out because of My name have said, "Let the Lord be glorified, and we will look on your gladness." Yet they themselves will be put to shame.
verses.66:6: The voice of the people from the city, a voice from the temple, the voice of the Lord repaying retribution to His enemies.
verses.66:7: Before she was in labor, she gave birth; before her delivery came, she gave birth to a male child.
verses.66:8: Who has ever heard such a thing? And who has seen anything like this? Will a land be in labor in one day, or will a nation be born at once, since Zion has been in labor and has given birth to her sons?
verses.66:9: "Will I, who cause others to give birth, Myself not give birth?" says the Lord. "If I am the one who grants childbearing to the rest, will I be barren?" says the Lord your God.
verses.66:10: Be glad with Jerusalem and exult in her, all you who love her; rejoice with her in joy, all of you who mourn over her,
verses.66:11: so that you may nurse and be filled from the breast of her comfort; so that you may draw milk and overflow with delights from her manifold glory.
verses.66:12: For this is what the Lord says: "Look, I will turn upon her like a river of peace, and like an overflowing torrent the glory of the nations, which you will nurse on: at the breasts you will be carried, and upon the knees they will caress you.
verses.66:13: Just as when a mother caresses someone, so I will comfort you, and in Jerusalem you will be comforted.
verses.66:14: You will see, and your heart will rejoice, and your bones will sprout like grass; and the hand of the Lord will be known to His servants, and He will be indignant toward His enemies.
verses.66:15: For look, the Lord will come in fire, and His chariots like a whirlwind, to render His fury in indignation and His rebuke in a flame of fire;
verses.66:16: for in fire the Lord will execute judgment, and by His sword against all flesh; and those killed by the Lord will be multiplied;
verses.66:17: those who were sanctifying themselves and considering themselves clean in the gardens behind the door inside, who were eating pig's flesh, and abomination, and the mouse: together they will be consumed," says the Lord.
verses.66:18: "Yet I am coming to gather their works and their thoughts, together with all nations and tongues; and they will come and see My glory.
verses.66:19: And I will set a sign among them, and I will send from among those who have been saved to the nations on the sea, to Africa and Lydia, aiming the arrow; to Italy and Greece, to the islands far away, to those who have not heard about Me and have not seen My glory. And they will proclaim My glory to the nations;
verses.66:20: and they will bring all your brothers from all the nations as a gift to the Lord, on horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and on mules, and in carriages, to My holy mountain Jerusalem," says the Lord, "just as when the sons of Israel bring an offering in a clean vessel into the house of the Lord.
verses.66:21: And I will take some from among them to be priests and Levites," says the Lord.
verses.66:22: "For just as the new heavens and the new earth, which I make to stand before Me," says the Lord, "so will your offspring and your name stand.
verses.66:23: And there will be month after month, and Sabbath after Sabbath: all flesh will come to worship before My face," says the Lord.
verses.66:24: "And they will go out and see the corpses of the men who transgressed against Me; their worm will not die, and their fire will not be extinguished; and they will be even to satiety of sight for all flesh."

notes.1:5: Vulgate "percutiam" ("should I strike", first-person singular active) presents God speaking directly, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a passive ("will you still be struck?"). Latin "super quo" can mean either "where [on the body]" or "on what account."
notes.1:9: Vulgate "semen" ("seed", matching the Septuagint and Romans 9:29) differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "survivors" or "remnant."
notes.1:18: Vulgate "arguite me" ("reprove Me" or "accuse Me", an active imperative with God as object) is a distinctive Latin reading compared to the Hebrew reciprocal "let us reason together."
notes.1:26: Vulgate "civitas justi" uses the singular substantive ("city of the righteous one" or "of what is right") rather than the abstract noun "city of righteousness" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.1:27: Vulgate "et reducent eam in justitia" ("and they will bring her back in righteousness") reads a finite verb with Zion as object, contrasting with the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "and her repentant ones with righteousness."
notes.2:4: Vulgate "conflabunt" ("will forge" or "melt down") and "exercebuntur" ("will be trained") are distinctive Latin renderings compared to the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "beat" and "learn."
notes.2:6: Vulgate "ut olim" ("as in former times") translates Hebrew "miqqedem" temporally rather than geographically ("from the east"), and "pueris alienis adhæserunt" ("clung to foreign children") contrasts with the Hebrew sense of striking bargains with foreigners.
notes.2:10: Vulgate "in fossa humo" ("in the dug-out ground") is a distinctive Latin rendering compared to "in the dust" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text; likewise in 2:19 and 2:21, Vulgate "percutere terram" ("to strike the earth") contrasts with Hebrew "to terrify the earth."
notes.2:20: Vulgate "talpas et vespertiliones" ("moles and bats") stands in the accusative case, serving as the object of "adoraret" or in apposition to the idols, rather than the dative ("cast ... to the moles and bats") found in translations of the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.3:1: Latin 'validum et fortem' ('the sturdy and the mighty') renders the Hebrew wordplay for 'support and staff' concretely as strong persons, before continuing with 'every support of bread and every support of water.'
notes.3:4: Latin 'effeminati' ('the effeminate') is a distinctly Vulgate rendering of a rare Hebrew term meaning 'capricious ones' or 'babes.'
notes.3:12: Latin 'qui te beatum dicunt' ('those who call you blessed') reflects an alternative vocalization of the Hebrew verb usually rendered 'those who guide you.'
notes.3:17: Latin 'crinem earum nudabit' ('will lay bare their hair') is a distinctly Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew is usually translated 'foreheads' or 'secret parts.'
notes.3:24: The Vulgate omits the Hebrew closing clause 'branding instead of beauty,' carrying the word for 'beauty' into 3:25 as 'Pulcherrimi' ('your most handsome men').
notes.4:3: Latin 'scriptus est in vita' ('written in life') uses the ablative case rather than the Hebrew 'written for life,' expressing inscription among the living.
notes.4:4: Latin 'Si' ('If') literally reproduces the Hebrew conditional particle that in context carries a temporal sense ('when').
notes.4:5: Latin 'ubi invocatus est' ('where He has been invoked') is a distinctly Vulgate rendering of the Hebrew term usually translated 'her assemblies.'
notes.5:1: Latin 'patruelis mei' ('of my cousin') translates a Hebrew kinsman term often rendered 'my beloved,' and 'in cornu filio olei' ('on a horn, the son of oil') preserves the Hebrew idiom for a fertile hilltop.
notes.5:7: Latin 'exspectavi' ('I waited') uses the first person singular directly as the Lord's voice, whereas the Hebrew has the third person ('he looked').
notes.5:9: Latin 'nisi' ('unless') literally renders the Hebrew elliptical oath formula meaning 'surely,' and in 5:10 Jerome converts the Hebrew measures into Roman equivalents ('jugera,' 'lagunculam,' and 'modii').
notes.5:17: Latin 'deserta in ubertatem versa' ('the desolate places that have been turned into fertility') is a distinctly Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew reads 'the ruins of the fat ones.'
notes.5:25: The Clementine Vulgate prints 'adversus' as an orthographic variant for 'aversus' ('turned away').
notes.6:1: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew for the hem or train of the Lord's robe neutrally as "the things that were beneath Him" (ea quae sub ipso erant).
notes.6:2: The Vulgate reads neuter "above it" (super illud, referring to the throne) and pairs plural verbs (velabant) with singular "His" (ejus), which Jerome and the Vulgate tradition understood as veiling the Lord's face and feet, whereas the Hebrew distributive singular refers to each seraph's own face and feet.
notes.6:5: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew verb (often translated "I am ruined/undone") from its homonymous root meaning "be silent" (quia tacui, "because I have kept silent").
notes.6:10: The Vulgate reads "Blind the heart" (Excaeca cor), where the Hebrew has "make fat/dull the heart."
notes.6:13: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text (which speaks of burning and a felled stump), the Vulgate presents a hopeful image: the remaining tenth "will be converted" (convertetur) and stand "for a display" (in ostensionem) like an oak "that spreads out its branches" (quae expandit ramos suos).
notes.7:1: The Clementine Vulgate places the break between verses 1 and 2 mid-clause, leaving "and they were not able" at the end of 7:1 and "to conquer it" at the start of 7:2.
notes.7:3: For the symbolic Hebrew name Shear-jashub ("a remnant shall return"), the Vulgate translates the first element into Latin ("he who is left behind," qui derelictus est) and retains the second as the name Jashub (Jasub).
notes.7:14: The Vulgate reads "a virgin" (virgo) and the passive "His name will be called" (vocabitur nomen ejus), aligning with the Septuagint and Matthew 1:23 rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's active "she will call."
notes.7:17: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew particle before "the king of Assyria" as the preposition "with" (cum rege Assyriorum) rather than as a direct-object marker ("namely, the king of Assyria").
notes.7:25: The Vulgate takes "the terror of thorns and briers" as the subject of a third-person verb ("will not come there," non veniet illuc), whereas the Hebrew is commonly read in the second person ("you will not go there for fear of briers and thorns").
notes.8:1: Both here (Velociter spolia detrahe, cito praedare) and in 8:3 (Accelera spolia detrahere; Festina praedari), the Vulgate translates the Hebrew symbolic name Maher-shalal-hash-baz directly into Latin rather than transliterating it.
notes.8:6: The Vulgate reads "has rather adopted" (assumpsit magis) Rezin and the son of Remaliah, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text is commonly translated "rejoices in" or "melts in fear before."
notes.8:21: The Clementine Vulgate prints suscipiet sursum, a traditional orthographic variant for suspiciet sursum ("will look upward"), parallel to "gaze at the earth" in 8:22.
notes.8:22: The Vulgate joins the opening clause of Hebrew 8:23 (English 9:1) to the end of 8:22 and derives its verb from the root "to fly," reading "and he will not be able to fly away from his anguish" (et non poterit avolare de angustia sua).
notes.8:23: Following Hebrew versification (corresponding to English 9:1), the Vulgate renders the Hebrew antithesis literally through passive verbs of weight, "was lightened" (alleviata est) versus "was weighed down" (aggravata est), where the Hebrew is commonly rendered "treated with contempt" versus "made glorious."
notes.9:1: Vulgate Isaiah 9:1-20 corresponds to 9:2-21 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text and most modern English versions, since Vulgate 8:23 corresponds to Hebrew 9:1.
notes.9:2: Latin 'et non magnificasti laetitiam' ("and have not magnified the joy") follows the Hebrew written text (Ketiv, "not") rather than the read tradition (Qere, "for it"); the Latin also specifies 'victores' ("victors").
notes.9:5: The Clementine Vulgate separates the first four titles with commas ('Admirabilis, Consiliarius, Deus, Fortis'), and 'Pater futuri saeculi' ("Father of the Age to Come") is a Vulgate-distinct rendering corresponding to Hebrew "Everlasting Father."
notes.9:13: Latin 'incurvantem et refrenantem' ("the one bowing down and the one restraining") is a distinctly Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew text has "palm branch and reed."
notes.10:15: Latin 'qui utique lignum est' ("which is indeed wood") is a distinctly Vulgate reading where the Hebrew has "what is not wood."
notes.10:18: Latin uses 'carmeli' as a common noun for "fruitful field" (orchard), and 'terrore profugus' ("a fugitive in terror") is a Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Hebrew has "as when a sick man wastes away."
notes.10:22: Latin 'consummatio abbreviata' ("a shortened completion," echoed in 10:23 'consummationem et abbreviationem') follows the phrasing reflected in Romans 9:28, whereas the Hebrew has "destruction is decreed."
notes.10:27: Latin 'a facie olei' ("before the face of the oil") renders the Hebrew word for fatness/oil specifically as "oil," a reading traditionally associated with anointing oil in Latin exegesis.
notes.10:33: Latin 'lagunculam' ("small flask") is a notable Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Hebrew text has "boughs" or "branches."
notes.11:2: Together with 11:3, the Vulgate distinguishes 'pietatis' ("piety") from 'timoris Domini' ("the fear of the Lord," which "will fill Him"), producing the traditional sevenfold enumeration where the Hebrew repeats "fear of the Lord."
notes.11:6: Latin reads 'ovis' ("sheep") in 11:6 and 'vitulus' ("calf") in 11:7 where the Hebrew has "fatling" and "cow"; in 11:8 'reguli' designates the basilisk.
notes.11:10: Latin 'sepulchrum ejus' ("His tomb") is a celebrated Vulgate-distinct reading where the Hebrew text has "his resting place."
notes.11:14: Latin uses 'Idumaea' (Idumea), the Greco-Latin name for Edom, and renders the Hebrew "westward" literally as 'per mare' ("by the sea").
notes.12:2: Vulgate reads salvator ("Savior") here and in 12:3 where the Hebrew has "salvation," while using in salutem ("salvation") at the end of 12:2; fiducialiter agam literally means "I will act confidently."
notes.12:4: Vulgate mementote ("remember") frames the command as recollection rather than the Hebrew causative "make mention" or "proclaim."
notes.12:6: Vulgate reads habitatio Sion ("dwelling of Zion"), an abstract or collective noun, rather than the Hebrew "inhabitant of Zion."
notes.13:1: Latin onus ("burden," also in 14:28) translates Hebrew massa ("oracle/pronouncement"); Vulgate spells Isaiah's father Amos (following the Greek) for Hebrew Amoz, distinct from the prophet Amos.
notes.13:2: Vulgate reads montem caliginosum ("dark" or "misty mountain"), connecting the Hebrew word with twilight/darkness rather than "bare mountain."
notes.13:12: Vulgate mundo obrizo ("pure refined gold") uses a technical Latin term for fire-tested gold where the Hebrew specifies "gold of Ophir."
notes.13:18: Vulgate lactantibus uteris literally reads "nursing wombs," corresponding to Hebrew "fruit of the womb."
notes.13:21: In 13:21-22, the Vulgate names the desert creatures draconibus ("dragons"), struthiones ("ostriches"), pilosi ("hairy creatures"), ululae ("owls"), and sirenes ("sirens," following the Septuagint), and renders the palaces as delubris ("temples/shrines").
notes.14:1: In the Clementine Vulgate, the opening sentence ("Its time is near to come, and its days will not be prolonged") begins chapter 14 rather than concluding 13:22 as in the Hebrew text.
notes.14:9: Latin Infernus (and inferos in 14:11, infernum in 14:15) literally denotes the lower realm or underworld (translating Hebrew Sheol); Vulgate gigantes ("giants," following the Septuagint) corresponds to Hebrew repha'im ("shades/departed spirits").
notes.14:11: Vulgate reads concidit cadaver tuum ("your corpse has fallen") and tinea ("moth"), diverging from the Hebrew "the sound of your harps" and "maggots."
notes.14:12: Latin Lucifer literally means "light-bearer" (the morning star), corresponding to Hebrew helel ("shining one"), with qui mane oriebaris ("who rose in the morning") corresponding to "son of the dawn." In 14:13, Vulgate monte testamenti ("mountain of the covenant") corresponds to Hebrew "mount of assembly."
notes.14:29: Vulgate regulus denotes the basilisk (a venomous serpent), and absorbens volucrem ("will swallow up the bird") is a distinctly Vulgate reading diverging from the Hebrew "flying fiery serpent."
notes.15:1: Latin "murus Moab" ("the wall of Moab") translates the Hebrew place name Kir-Moab literally; "conticuit" ("fell silent") renders a Hebrew verb that can mean either "be silenced" or "be destroyed."
notes.15:3: Latin "omnis ululatus descendit in fletum" ("all wailing goes down into weeping") takes the noun "wailing" as the subject, differing from the Hebrew ("everyone wails, going down in weeping").
notes.15:5: Latin "vectes ejus" ("its bars") translates the Hebrew as "bars/bolts" rather than "fugitives," and "vitulam conternantem" ("a three-year-old heifer") renders Hebrew Eglath-shelishiyah as a descriptive phrase rather than a proper name.
notes.15:7: Vulgate-distinct reading: "Secundum magnitudinem operis, et visitatio eorum: ad torrentem Salicum ducent eos" renders the Hebrew terms for stored wealth and carrying it away as "the greatness of the work," "their visitation," and "they will lead them."
notes.15:8: The Vulgate reads the place name "Gallim" here instead of Hebrew Eglaim, and in 15:9 reads "Dibon" instead of Hebrew Dimon.
notes.16:1: Vulgate-distinct reading: "Emitte agnum, Domine, dominatorem terrae, de petra deserti" addresses the Lord with a singular imperative, places "the ruler of the earth" in apposition to "the lamb," and translates Hebrew Sela literally as "the rock."
notes.16:4: Vulgate-distinct readings: "profugi mei" ("My fugitives") is addressed to Moab, while "pulvis" ("the dust") and "miser" ("the wretched one") differ from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("the extortioner" and "destruction").
notes.16:7: Latin "muros cocti lateris" ("the walls of baked brick") translates the Hebrew place name Kir-hareseth literally (as also in 16:11), and "his qui laetantur ... loquimini plagas suas" differs markedly from the Hebrew ("for the raisin cakes ... moan, utterly stricken").
notes.16:10: The Vulgate renders Hebrew karmel ("orchard" or "fruitful field") as the proper name "Carmel."
notes.17:3: Latin "adjutorium" ("help") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "fortress."
notes.17:6: Latin "fructus ejus" ("its fruit") reflects reading the Hebrew as "its fruit" rather than "a fruitful tree"; in 17:5 "quod restiterit" ("what remains") similarly differs from Hebrew "standing grain."
notes.17:9: Latin "aratra, et segetes" ("plows and grainfields") is a Vulgate-distinct rendering of a difficult Hebrew phrase often translated "wooded heights and summit" (or in the Septuagint, "the Hivites and the Amorites"); in 17:8 "lucos et delubra" ("groves and shrines") renders Hebrew Asherah poles and incense altars.
notes.17:11: Vulgate-distinct readings: "labrusca" ("a wild vine") and "in die haereditatis" ("on the day of inheritance," reading Hebrew nachalah as "inheritance" rather than "sickness/grief"), following "plantationem fidelem" ("a faithful planting") in 17:10.
notes.17:13: The Latin shifts to singular pronouns ("eum ... fugiet ... rapietur," rendered "it") for the collective multitude and translates Hebrew galgal ("whirling dust/chaff") as "turbo" ("a whirlwind"); in 17:14 "in matutino" ("in the morning") contrasts with Hebrew "before morning."
notes.18:1: Latin "cymbalo alarum" ("cymbal of wings") is a distinctive Vulgate rendering of a rare Hebrew phrase often translated "whirring wings" or "shadowing wings."
notes.18:2: The Vulgate renders the difficult Hebrew descriptions of the Ethiopian nation as "uprooted and torn to pieces," "after whom there is no other," and "waiting and trampled down" (repeated in 18:7), where modern translations from the Masoretic Text often read "tall and smooth," "feared near and far," and "mighty and conquering."
notes.18:4: The Vulgate reads "as the midday light is clear" and "in the day of harvest" (in die messis), whereas the Masoretic Text has "like clear heat in sunshine" and "in the heat of harvest."
notes.18:5: Latin "immatura perfectio" ("unripe perfection") literally renders a Hebrew expression for a ripening sour grape; similarly in 18:6 the Vulgate reads "aestate perpetua" ("in perpetual summer").
notes.19:10: The Vulgate reads "its irrigated grounds will droop: all who made ponds to catch fish" for a difficult Hebrew verse often translated "her weavers [or pillars] will be crushed, and all who work for wages will be grieved."
notes.19:11: Latin "Taneos" (Tanis, also in 19:13) is the Greco-Latin name for the Egyptian city called Zoan in Hebrew.
notes.19:15: The Vulgate construes "head and tail" as direct objects and renders the Hebrew botanical pair ("palm branch and reed") as "the one bending down and the one restraining" (incurvantem et refrenantem).
notes.19:18: Latin "Civitas solis" ("City of the Sun," i.e., Heliopolis) reflects the Hebrew textual reading Ir ha-Cheres (attested also in the Dead Sea Scrolls), whereas the standard Masoretic Text reads Ir ha-Heres ("City of Destruction").
notes.19:23: Latin "servient Aegyptii Assur" ("the Egyptians will serve Assyria") follows the Septuagint in taking Assyria as the object of service, whereas many modern translations from Hebrew render it "the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians."
notes.20:1: The Clementine Vulgate reads "Thathan" (corresponding to Hebrew Tartan, an Assyrian military title meaning commander-in-chief) and "Azotum" (Azotus, the Greco-Latin name for Ashdod).
notes.20:3: The Vulgate connects "of three years" (trium annorum) to the future "sign and wonder" rather than to the duration of Isaiah's walking naked and barefoot, as commonly construed in translations from the Masoretic Text.
notes.20:6: Latin "insulae hujus" ("of this island") is a literal rendering of a Hebrew term that can denote either an island or a coastal region ("coastland").
notes.21:3: The Vulgate reads corrui cum audirem, conturbatus sum cum viderem ("I collapsed when I heard; I was thrown into turmoil when I saw"), whereas the Hebrew describes being too bowed down to hear and too dismayed to see.
notes.21:4: A striking Vulgate-distinct reading: Babylon dilecta mea posita est mihi in miraculum ("Babylon, my beloved, has been turned into a wonder for me"), where the Hebrew speaks of the longed-for twilight being turned into trembling.
notes.21:8: Following the consonantal Hebrew text (aryeh), the Vulgate reads clamavit leo ("a lion cried out"), referring figuratively to the watchman rather than emending to "the lookout."
notes.21:13: The Vulgate translates in semitis ("on the paths"), taking the Hebrew noun in the sense of "paths" rather than "caravans."
notes.22:5: A Vulgate-distinct reading: scrutans murum, et magnificus super montem ("searching the wall and magnificent upon the mountain"), whereas the Hebrew depicts breaking down walls and crying out to the mountain.
notes.22:6: The Vulgate renders parietem nudavit clypeus ("the shield laid bare the wall"), translating Hebrew Qir as the common noun "wall" (parietem) and making "shield" (clypeus) the subject rather than "Kir uncovered the shield."
notes.22:14: The Latin uses the literal Semitic oath idiom Si dimittetur ("If it will be forgiven..."), an elliptical curse-oath expressing emphatic negation ("Certainly it will not be forgiven"), and distinctly includes vox ("the voice") of the Lord of hosts.
notes.22:15: The Vulgate renders Shebna's title as qui habitat in tabernaculo ("who dwells in the tabernacle") and praepositum templi ("the overseer of the temple"), whereas the Hebrew refers to the royal steward over the palace.
notes.22:17: The Vulgate distinctly renders Hebrew gaver in its later sense as gallus gallinaceus ("rooster") rather than "strong man," and in 22:18 reads Coronas coronabit te tribulatione ("He will crown you with crowns, with tribulation").
notes.23:1: Throughout this oracle (23:1, 6, 10, 14), the Vulgate renders Hebrew Tarshish as mare ("sea" or "seas"), and here reads domus unde venire consueverant ("the house from which they used to come") where the Hebrew says "without house or entering."
notes.23:3: The Vulgate explicitly identifies Hebrew Shihor as Nili ("the Nile").
notes.23:13: A notable Vulgate-distinct reading: Assur fundavit eam; in captivitatem traduxerunt robustos ejus ("Assyria founded it; they led away its strong men into captivity"), where the Hebrew speaks of Assyria assigning the land to desert creatures and erecting siege towers.
notes.23:18: The Vulgate translates usque ad vetustatem ("until old age"), taking the Hebrew adjective for "stately" or "fine" clothing in the temporal sense of lasting into old age.
notes.24:6: Vulgate reads "will sin" (peccabunt) and "will go mad" (insanient), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "bear guilt" and "are scorched."
notes.24:14: Vulgate has the temporal clause "when the Lord has been glorified" (cum glorificatus fuerit Dominus) and hinnient (literally "will neigh," Jerome's literal rendering of the Hebrew verb used both for neighing and for a ringing cry).
notes.24:15: Vulgate reads "in teachings" (in doctrinis), taking the Hebrew term meaning "in the lights" (understood of the regions of light, the east) in the sense of illuminations or doctrines.
notes.24:16: Vulgate reads "My secret to me" (Secretum meum mihi), taking the Hebrew razi-li in the sense of "secret" or "mystery" rather than "leanness" ("I waste away").
notes.24:22: Vulgate reads "of a single bundle" (unius fascis) where the Hebrew reads "of a prisoner"; similarly in 24:20 Vulgate has "carried off like a tent of a single night" (auferetur quasi tabernaculum unius noctis) for Hebrew "sways like a hut."
notes.25:1: Vulgate closes the verse with the transliteration "Amen" (Amen), rendering the Hebrew noun meaning "firmness" or "truth."
notes.25:4: Vulgate reads "a hope from the whirlwind" (spes a turbine) where the Hebrew has "a refuge from the storm"; in 25:5 Vulgate likewise has "under a scorching cloud" (sub nube torrente) and "offshoot" (propaginem) for Hebrew "by the shadow of a cloud" and "song."
notes.25:7: Vulgate renders Hebrew "will swallow up" as "will cast down headlong" (praecipitabit, also in 25:8) and uses the active clause "which He has woven" (quam orditus est) where the Hebrew has a passive participle ("which is woven").
notes.25:10: Vulgate reads "beneath Him" (sub eo, repeated in 25:11, referring to the Lord) and "in a wagon" (in plaustro), whereas the Hebrew reads "in its place" and "in the water of a dung-pit."
notes.26:1: Vulgate explicitly names "Zion" (Sion) and reads personal "a savior" (salvator) where the Hebrew has "We have a strong city; He sets salvation as walls and rampart."
notes.26:3: Vulgate reads "The old error has departed" (Vetus error abiit) for the Hebrew "a steadfast mind"; in 26:4 Vulgate likewise uses the past indicative "You have hoped" (Sperastis) where the Hebrew has an imperative ("Trust").
notes.26:11: Vulgate renders the clause with subjunctives ("let Your hand be lifted up, and let them not see") and "the envious peoples" (zelantes populi) where the Hebrew has "Your hand is lifted up, yet they do not see; let them see Your zeal for the people."
notes.26:15: Vulgate reads "You have shown indulgence to the nation" (Indulsisti genti) and frames the next clause as a rhetorical question ("have You been glorified?", numquid glorificatus es?), where the Hebrew reads "You have increased the nation ... You are glorified."
notes.26:19: Vulgate reads "You will pull down the land of the giants into ruin" (terram gigantum detrahes in ruinam) where the Hebrew has "the earth will give birth to the shades"; gigantes ("giants," as in 26:14) renders Hebrew rephaim.
notes.27:1: Vulgate renders Hebrew bariach ("fleeing" or "swift") as vectem ("bar" or "bolt"), giving "the bar serpent."
notes.27:2: Vulgate reads vinea meri ("the vineyard of pure wine") as the nominative subject singing to the Lord (cantabit ei), whereas the Hebrew has a plural imperative, "Sing of her!"
notes.27:4: Vulgate translates the Hebrew dative suffix ("to me") as a direct-object accusative (dabit me spinam et veprem), yielding "Who will make Me a thorn and a bramble in battle?" rather than "Who would give me thorns and briers?"
notes.27:8: Vulgate translates Hebrew hagah (which can mean "remove" or "meditate") as meditatus est ("He has meditated") and qadim ("east wind") as aestus ("heat").
notes.27:11: Vulgate renders Hebrew qetsirah ("its boughs") as messes ("her harvests") and me'irot otah ("set fire to it") as docentes eam ("teaching her").
notes.28:2: Vulgate makes Dominus the nominative subject ("the Lord is mighty and strong"), whereas the Hebrew describes a mighty and strong agent belonging to the Lord.
notes.28:10: Vulgate renders the Hebrew rhythmic repetition (tsav latsav ... qav laqav) with paired Latin imperatives (manda, remanda; exspecta, reexspecta) and translates both final adverbs identically as ibi ("there").
notes.28:20: Vulgate presents the proverb as a bed too narrow for two so that one falls off and a short cloak unable to cover both (alter ... utrumque), differing from the Hebrew image of one person unable to stretch out or wrap up.
notes.28:21: Vulgate translates the Hebrew place name Har Perazim ("Mount Perazim") literally into Latin as in monte divisionum ("on the mountain of divisions").
notes.28:28: Vulgate ungulis suis (literally "with his hooves") renders Hebrew parashaw ("his horses"), referring to the hooves of the farmer's threshing animals.
notes.29:1: Vulgate translates Hebrew chanah ("encamped") as expugnavit ("conquered") and renders the following verb in the passive indicative (additus est, "has been added") rather than as an imperative.
notes.29:3: Vulgate renders Hebrew kaddur ("in a circle") literally as quasi sphaeram ("like a sphere").
notes.29:5: Vulgate translates Hebrew zarayik ("your strangers/foes") from the root for winnowing as ventilantium te ("those winnowing you"), and mots ("chaff") as favilla ("ash").
notes.29:17: Vulgate leaves the Hebrew term carmel ("orchard" or "fruitful field," also the name of Mount Carmel) untranslated alongside Libanus (Lebanon).
notes.29:23: Vulgate renders Hebrew ya'aritsu ("they will stand in awe of") as praedicabunt ("they will proclaim"), and in 29:24 renders leqach ("instruction") as legem ("the law").
notes.30:4: Tanis renders Vulgate Tani, the Greco-Latin name (via the Septuagint) for the Egyptian city called Zoan in Hebrew.
notes.30:7: Vulgate Superbia tantum est, quiesce ("It is mere pride; be still") renders Hebrew Rahab hem shavet ("Rahab who sits still") by translating the poetic name Rahab as "pride" and taking the final word as an imperative.
notes.30:13: Vulgate et requisita ("and sought out") is a distinct reading in which Jerome translated the Hebrew verb for "bulging out" through its homonym meaning "to seek."
notes.30:20: Vulgate panem arctum, et aquam brevem denotes "scant/narrow bread and scarce/short water" (Hebrew: "bread of adversity and water of affliction"), and non faciet avolare ("will not cause to fly away") renders the Hebrew verb "hide himself" via its root meaning "wing."
notes.30:33: Vulgate a rege praeparata reads "prepared by the king" (ablative of agent), whereas the Hebrew reads "prepared for the king."
notes.31:6: Vulgate sicut in profundum recesseratis ("just as you had withdrawn into the depths") differs from the Hebrew, which reads "to Him against whom you have deeply revolted."
notes.31:8: Vulgate non a facie gladii ("not from before the sword") reflects reading the Hebrew lo ("for himself") as the homophonous negative lo ("not").
notes.31:9: Vulgate fortitudo ejus ("its strength") renders Hebrew salo ("its rock/crag") figuratively as strength.
notes.32:8: Vulgate super duces ("over leaders") takes Hebrew nedivot ("noble things") as a personal plural denoting nobles or rulers.
